# Router benchmark step 1: RouterBench (2026-11-26)

- Who: Martian (+ UC Berkeley), March 2024. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12031
- Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/withmartian/routerbench (1.47 GB; files `routerbench_0shot.pkl` 99.6 MB, `routerbench_5shot.pkl` 171 MB, `routerbench_raw.pkl` 1.2 GB; `routerbench_rag.pkl` was deleted). No licence shown.
- Size: 405,467 samples (question × model) = ~36.5k prompts × 11 models. Each row: prompt, model answer, cost, score (right/wrong or 0–1).

## Sub-benchmarks (8 = 7 public + 1 RAG)
| Area | Benchmark | Prompts (HF data) |
|---|---|---|
| Knowledge | MMLU (57 subjects) | 14,042 |
| Commonsense | HellaSwag | 10,042 |
| Commonsense | ARC-Challenge | 1,470 |
| Commonsense | Winogrande | 1,267 |
| Math | GSM8K | 7,450 |
| Code | MBPP | 427 |
| Conversation | MT-Bench | 80 |
| Other small tasks | ~20 small sets (not identified) | 1,719 |
| RAG (paper only) | Martian client search queries (sports, history, media & art, politics) | 800 — not in HF file |
| **Total** | | **~36,497** |

Counts from my earlier HF analysis (`sn34_benchmark_question_counts_2026-11-23.md`). The paper says "8 datasets, 64 tasks" (a figure caption says 77 subsets); the per-dataset counts are not in the paper text.

## Models (11 + 3 RAG-only)
- Open (6): Llama-2-70B-chat, Mixtral-8x7B-chat, Yi-34B-chat, Code Llama-34B, Mistral-7B-chat, WizardLM-13B
- API (5): GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo, Claude-instant-v1, Claude-v1, Claude-v2
- RAG-only (3): sonar-small-online, sonar-medium-online (Perplexity), You.com API

## For Yugos
- Overlap: MMLU-style (Yugos uses MMLU-Pro), GSM8K, ARC (challenge/easy), Winogrande, HellaSwag, MBPP — all in Yugos's benchmark list.
- But all models are from 2023 → labels don't transfer to GPT-6 / Claude 5.x.
- Questions are easy for today's models → routing gain is small.
- Use: learning the method (AIQ metric, cost-quality curve) and as extra questions; not as labels.

# Router benchmark step 2: RouterEval (2026-11-26)

- Who: Zhongzhan Huang, Guoming Ling, Yupei Lin, Yandong Chen, Shanshan Zhong, Hefeng Wu, Liang Lin (Sun Yat-sen Univ. group (unverified)). EMNLP 2025 Findings. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10657 · https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.208/
- Code: https://github.com/MilkThink-Lab/RouterEval (MIT).
- Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/linggm/RouterEval (MIT). Also on Google Drive and Baidu Drive.
  - `leaderboard_score.zip` 83.8 MB → `leaderboard_old.pkl` (1.15 GB), `leaderboard_new.pkl` (293 MB), `leaderboard_mmlu_pro.pkl` (176 MB). Checked by listing the zip.
  - `leaderboard_prompt.zip` 51.5 MB → 3 matching `*_prompt.pkl` files. Checked by listing the zip.
  - `leaderboard_embed.zip` 457 MB (embeddings: longformer, RoBERTa, RoBERTa-last, Sentence-BERT).
  - `router_dataset.zip` 267 MB (ready train/val/test sets for the 12 tasks).
  - `full_data/` (~400 GB): 12 folders, one zip per model, e.g. `01-ai__Yi-1.5-34B-Chat-details_876.zip`. Each holds one `.pkl` with the raw answers.
- Format: **everything is Python pickle**. There is no CSV/JSON/parquet. I did not unpickle anything, so columns are not checked.
- Size: 200M+ score records. 8,576 LLMs in total (1,823–5,000 per benchmark). 12 benchmarks. Split 8:1:1 into train/val/test.
- Source of the models: the file names (`old` / `new`, `<org>__<model>-details`) match Hugging Face's Open LLM Leaderboard v1 and v2 "details" sets. The paper does not say this. (unverified)

## Sub-benchmarks (12)
| Area | Benchmark | LLMs scored | Test prompts (paper Table 4) | Full set (likely, ≈10× test) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commonsense | ARC (Challenge) | 5,000 | 118 | ~1,172 (unverified) |
| Commonsense | HellaSwag | 5,000 | 1,005 | ~10,042 (unverified) |
| Knowledge | MMLU | 5,000 | 1,430 | ~14,042 (unverified) |
| Knowledge | TruthfulQA | 5,000 | 82 | ~817 (unverified) |
| Commonsense | Winogrande | 5,000 | 127 | ~1,267 (unverified) |
| Math | GSM8K | 5,000 | 132 | ~1,319 (unverified) |
| Instruction following | IFEval | 3,811 | 55 | ~541 (unverified) |
| Reasoning | BBH | 3,811 | 577 | ~5,761 (unverified) |
| Science | GPQA (main+diamond+extended mix) | 3,811 | 120 | ~1,192 (unverified) |
| Reasoning | MuSR | 3,811 | 76 | ~756 (unverified) |
| Math | MATH Level 5 | 3,811 | 136 | ~1,324 (unverified) |
| Knowledge | MMLU-Pro | 1,823 | 1,204 | ~12,032 (unverified) |
| **Total** | | **8,576 unique** | **5,062** | **~50,265 (unverified)** |

- Test counts are from the paper. The paper lists the 12th set as "MMMU-PRO" in Table 4. That is a typo for MMLU-Pro.
- The full-set guess = the official size of each set. Each is almost exactly 10× the test count. That fits an 8:1:1 split of the full leaderboard sets.
- The first 6 sets = Open LLM Leaderboard v1. The last 6 = Open LLM Leaderboard v2. (unverified)

## Models (8,576)
- Almost all are open models from 2023–2024. Most are ~7B. Many are community fine-tunes and merges.
- Example names seen in `full_data/`: `0-hero/Matter-0.2-7B-DPO`, `01-ai/Yi-1.5-34B`, `01-ai/Yi-1.5-34B-Chat`, `01-ai/Yi-1.5-34B-Chat-16K`.
- No closed API models are in the pool. GPT-4 / GPT-3.5 / GPT-4 Turbo / Qwen1.5-32B appear only as "reference" scores.
- Reference scores used: GPT-4 0.953 HellaSwag, 0.864 MMLU, 0.875 Winogrande, 0.920 GSM8K, 0.769 IFEval, 0.830 BBH, 0.397 GPQA, 0.699 MuSR, 0.400 MATH L5. GPT-3.5 0.852 ARC. Qwen1.5-32B 0.669 TruthfulQA. GPT-4 Turbo 0.637 MMLU-Pro.

## How it tests routers
- Pool sizes: easy m = 3 or 5. Hard m = 10, 100 or 1,000.
- 3 pool types: all-strong (top 20%), all-weak (bottom 20%), strong-to-weak (one per rank band). Only models scoring 0.1–0.9 are used.
- Metrics: μo (score of picked models), VB (μo ÷ best single model in pool), VR (μo ÷ reference model like GPT-4), Ep (entropy of choices; near 0 = router always picks the same model).
- Baselines: oracle, random, r_o(0.5) (oracle half the time), LinearR, MLPR, kNN, C-RoBERTa, MLC.

## Key findings
- "Model-level scaling up": a good router gets better as the pool grows. The oracle beats the best single model a lot.
  - Oracle VB at m=3: ARC 1.34, MMLU 1.35, TruthfulQA 1.21, GPQA 2.00, MATH L5 1.33.
  - Even an all-weak pool (each ≤0.3 on MMLU) gets near GPT-4 level with an oracle.
- 3–10 candidate models are already enough for most of the gain.
- Real routers are far from the oracle. Most have VB ≤ 1 (worse than just using the best model). Example: LinearR on ARC m=3 has VB 0.96.
- Some routers collapse to one model (Ep ≈ 0).

## For Yugos
- Overlap with Yugos list: MMLU-Pro, GPQA (not Diamond-only), MuSR, ARC-Challenge, Winogrande, HellaSwag, GSM8K, MATH (Level 5 only). BBH is the older form of BBEH.
- No code, no agentic tasks, no HLE/SimpleQA/AIME.
- Model freshness: very old. No GPT-6 / Claude 5.x / Gemini 4 / DeepSeek V4. No GPT-5 either. Labels do not transfer to Yugos models.
- Effort data: none. One score per model per question.
- Big practical risk: all data is pickle. Only load it in a throw-away sandbox. Never on a machine with keys or wallets.
- Use: the scaling idea ("3–10 good models are enough") and the VB / Ep metrics. Also a big pool to test "does the router collapse to one model". Not useful as labels for Yugos.

# Router benchmark step 3: LLMRouterBench (2026-11-26)

- Who: Hao Li, Yiqun Zhang, Zhaoyan Guo, Chenxu Wang, Shengji Tang, Qiaosheng Zhang, Yang Chen, Biqing Qi, Peng Ye, Lei Bai, Zhen Wang, Shuyue Hu. Northwestern Polytechnical Univ. + Shanghai AI Lab. Jan 2026. README says Findings of ACL 2026. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.07206
- Code: https://github.com/ynulihao/LLMRouterBench (MIT).
- Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/NPULH/LLMRouterBench (MIT `LICENSE` file in the repo). One file: `bench-release.tar.gz` (1.28 GB, 1,455 entries). Also on Google Drive and Baidu.
- Format: plain JSON. Path = `bench-release/<dataset>/<split>/<model>/<name>-<timestamp>.json`. Checked by streaming the tarball and opening 7 files.
  - Top-level keys: `performance`, `time_taken`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cost`, `counts`, `model_name`, `dataset_name`, `split`, `demo`, `data_fingerprint`, `records`.
  - Per question (`records`): `index`, `origin_query`, `prompt`, `prediction`, `ground_truth`, `score` (0/1 or 0–1), `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cost` (USD), `raw_output` (full answer; tau2 = full chat log).
- Size: 391,645 results (paper text; table rows sum to 391,120). 23,945 prompts (table sum 23,926). ~1.8B tokens. Cost: $2,772 API + ~1,000 A800 GPU-hours.

## Sub-benchmarks (21 in paper + 4 extra in the release)
| Area | Benchmark | Prompts | Setting |
|---|---|---|---|
| Math | AIME | 60 | both |
| Math | MATH500 | 500 | performance |
| Math | MATHBench | 150 | performance |
| Math | LiveMathBench | 121 | cost |
| Code | HumanEval | 164 | performance |
| Code | MBPP | 974 | performance |
| Code | LiveCodeBench | 1,055 | both |
| Agent / code | SWE-bench **Verified** | 500 | cost |
| Agent | tau2-bench (airline 50, retail 114, telecom 114) | 278 | cost |
| Logic | BBH | 1,080 | performance |
| Logic | KORBench | 1,250 | performance |
| Logic | Knights & Knaves | 700 | performance |
| Knowledge | MMLU-Pro | 1,000 (perf) + 3,000 (cost) | both |
| Knowledge | GPQA (Diamond) | 198 | both |
| Knowledge | HLE | 2,158 (+ a 500 subset) | cost |
| Knowledge | SimpleQA | 4,326 (+ a 500 subset) | cost |
| Knowledge | FinQA | 1,147 | performance |
| Knowledge | MedQA | 1,273 | performance |
| Emotion | EmoryNLP | 697 | performance |
| Emotion | MELD | 1,232 | performance |
| Chat / instructions | ArenaHard | 750 (split into coding / creative_writing / math files too) | cost (release also has the 20 small models) |
| *Extra in release* | ARC-Challenge | 1,172 | 20 small models only |
| *Extra in release* | Winogrande (valid) | 1,267 | 20 small models only |
| *Extra in release* | ARC-AGI v1 | 400 | 17 API runs |
| **Total (paper)** | | **23,926–23,945** | |

- Counts are from the README and paper. I checked these inside the files: GPQA 198, MMLU-Pro 1,001 and 3,000, tau2 278, ARC-C 1,172, Winogrande 1,267, ARC-AGI 400.
- tau2 domains: the 278 tasks are in file order 50 airline, then 114 retail, then 114 telecom. No banking. I found this by reading task text. The paper does not list it.
- SWE-bench: folder name is `swe-bench/verified`. Scaffold is not stated in the paper (unverified).
- ArenaHard: 750 prompts and coding / creative-writing / math parts match Arena-Hard **v2.0**. The paper does not name the version or judge. (unverified)
- GPQA 198 = the Diamond size. (unverified that it is exactly Diamond)

## Models (33 in paper + extras in release)
- Performance setting, 20 small open models (~7–9B), run locally on vLLM, temp 0.2:
  - DeepHermes-3-Llama-3-8B-Preview, DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Fin-R1, GLM-Z1-9B-0414, Intern-S1-mini, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-UltraMedical, Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Nano-8B-v1, MiMo-7B-RL-0530, MiniCPM4.1-8B, NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2, OpenThinker3-7B, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B, Cogito-v1-preview-llama-8B, Gemma-2-9b-it, GLM-4-9b-chat, Granite-3.3-8b-instruct, InternLM3-8b-instruct
- Performance-cost setting, 13 API models (via OpenRouter; GLM-4.6 and Intern-S1 via own APIs):
  - OpenAI: GPT-5-chat, GPT-5 (medium effort; file `gpt-5-medium`)
  - Anthropic: Claude-sonnet-4
  - Google: Gemini-2.5-flash, Gemini-2.5-pro
  - DeepSeek: DeepSeek-v3-0324, DeepSeek-v3.1-terminus, DeepSeek-r1-0528
  - Qwen: Qwen3-235b-a22b-2507, Qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking-2507
  - Others: GLM-4.6, Kimi-k2-0905, Intern-s1
- Extra folders in the release (not in the paper): `openrouter` (OpenRouter auto-router, 13 datasets), `gpt-4.1` (6 sets), `qwen3-235b-a22b-thinking` / `-no-thinking` (older Qwen3, 7–8 sets), `intern-s1-new` (7 sets), `claude-opus-4.1` (SWE-bench only).
- tau2 has 12 of the 13 API models (no GPT-5-chat).

## Router baselines (10)
- RouterDC, EmbedLLM, MODEL-SAT, Avengers, HybridLLM, FrugalGPT, RouteLLM, GraphRouter, Avengers-Pro, OpenRouter.

## Key findings
- Models really are complementary. No single small model wins every area.
- Many routers score about the same. Avengers (no training) matches the trained ones.
- Best routers: up to ~4% better than the best single model (GPT-5). Or 31.7% cheaper at the same accuracy.
- OpenRouter's auto-router is ~24.7% worse than GPT-5 alone.
- Big gap to the oracle. Main reason: routers fail to pick the few models that get hard questions right.
  - On 410 hard test questions (≤3 models right), Avengers gets 24.6%, EmbedLLM 23.2%.
- Embedding model barely matters (a 22.7M MiniLM ≈ a 7B gte-Qwen2).
- A few carefully chosen models beat a big random pool.
- Latency differs a lot: Qwen3-Thinking ~262 s vs GLM-4.6 ~32 s at similar accuracy.

## For Yugos
- Overlap with Yugos list (most of any router set): MMLU-Pro, GPQA Diamond, HLE, SimpleQA, MedQA, ARC-Challenge, Winogrande, Arena-Hard (v2, unverified), AIME, MATH (MATH500), LiveCodeBench, HumanEval, MBPP, SWE-bench Verified, tau2 (airline, retail, telecom). BBH is the older form of BBEH.
- Missing: BBEH, MuSR, LiveBench, ARC-Easy, HellaSwag, LongBench v2, GSM8K, ArXivMath, BigCodeBench, DS-1000, CRUXEval, Terminal-Bench, BFCL, tau2 banking.
- Model freshness: late-2025 (GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5, DeepSeek V3.1/R1). Two generations behind GPT-6 / Claude 5.x / Gemini 4 / DeepSeek V4.
- Effort data: only coarse pairs. GPT-5 medium vs GPT-5-chat. Qwen3 thinking vs instruct. DeepSeek R1 vs V3. No low/high sweep.
- Very useful: real per-question cost and token counts, and full tau2 chat logs.
- How to use:
  - Use the questions (with gold answers) as the Yugos-style eval pool. Re-run them on current models.
  - Use the 2025 labels to pre-train a "question difficulty" or "which family wins" feature.
  - Use tau2 logs to study where agents fail per domain.
  - Do not trust old model labels for new models.

# Router benchmark step 4: RouterArena (2026-11-26)

- Who: Yifan Lu, Rixin Liu, Jiayi Yuan, Xingqi Cui, Shenrun Zhang, Hongyi Liu, Jiarong Xing. Rice University. ICLR 2026. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00202
- Code + live leaderboard: https://github.com/RouteWorks/RouterArena (Apache-2.0) · site https://routeworks.github.io
- Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/RouteWorks/RouterArena (no licence on the HF card). 3 parquet files:
  - `data/full-00000-of-00001.parquet` 3.7 MB = 8,400 questions
  - `data/sub_10-00000-of-00001.parquet` 0.4 MB = 809 questions (10% subset for local tests)
  - `data/robustness-00000-of-00001.parquet` 0.2 MB = 420 noisy re-written questions (typos, paraphrase)
- Columns: `Category`, `Domain`, `Dataset name`, `Global Index`, `Context`, `Question`, `Options`, `Answer`, `Metadata`, `Keywords` (always empty), `Difficulty`.
- **Questions only.** No model answers in the HF data.
- Model answers live in the GitHub repo instead:
  - `cached_results/`: only 3 models (claude-3-haiku-20240307, gemini-2.0-flash-001, gpt-4o-mini), 809 `sub_10` rows each, JSONL.
  - `router_inference/predictions/`: one JSON per submitted router (36 main files + robustness files, 14–28 MB each). Each row: `global index`, `prompt`, `prediction` (= model the router chose), `generated_result` (answer, tokens, provider, sometimes `thinking_config`), `accuracy`, `cost`. Checked by download.
- Rules: evaluation only. Routers may not train on RouterArena data or route by dataset name.

## Sub-benchmarks (23 sources, 8,400 questions)
| Area | Benchmark | Prompts |
|---|---|---|
| Knowledge | MMLU-Pro (14 subjects) | 2,528 |
| Trivia | OpenTDB (24 categories) | 887 |
| Trivia | QANTA (quiz bowl) | 644 |
| Medicine | PubMedQA | 466 |
| Language | SuperGLUE (WiC, RC, QA, Entailment, Cloze, WSC, Causal) | 443 |
| Library science | ArcMMLU | 396 |
| Code | LiveCodeBench | 385 |
| Reading | NarrativeQA | 383 |
| Geography | GeoBench | 330 |
| Medicine | MedMCQA | 304 |
| Ethics | ETHICS (commonsense, virtue, deontology, justice) | 283 |
| Translation | WMT19 (gu/de/zh/cs/fi/lt/kk/ru → en) | 257 |
| Music | MusicTheoryBench | 221 |
| Knowledge | MMLU (formal logic, management) | 181 |
| Math | MathQA | 158 |
| Games | ChessInstruct | 148 |
| Math | AsDiv | 88 |
| Finance | FinQA | 74 |
| Commonsense | SocialIQA | 61 |
| Math | MATH | 55 |
| Geography | GeoGraphyData_100k | 45 |
| Math | AIME | 39 |
| Math | GSM8K | 24 |
| **Total** | | **8,400** |

- Counts are from the HF dataset server (`Dataset name` column, 79 sub-labels merged into 23 sources). Checked.
- 9 domains (Dewey Decimal, no religion): 3 at 1,400 (CS/general, science, technology) and 6 at 700.
- Difficulty (by how many of 42 models solved it): easy 3,990 (≥20/42), medium 2,445 (5–19), hard 1,965 (≤4).
- Built from ~62k raw questions → ~30k → balanced and de-duplicated to 8,400. Bloom levels set by DeepSeek-V3.1.

## Models
- **Paper difficulty pool (42, answers not released):** gpt-5, claude-3.5-sonnet, deepseek-chat, gpt-4o, llama-3.1-405b-instruct, glm-4-plus, gpt-4-1106-preview, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (×2), Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, QwQ-32B, gpt-4o-mini, Llama-3-70B-Instruct, gemini-flash-1.5, glm-4-air, Qwen1.5-72B-Chat, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, glm-4-flash, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct, Yi-34B-Chat, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (×2), Nous-Hermes-2-Yi-34B, Llama-2-70b-chat (×2), Ministral-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-3B-instruct, dolphin-2.9-llama3-8b, Qwen2.5-32B, Mistral-7B-Instruct v0.2 / v0.3, Llama-3-8B-Instruct (×2), dolphin-2.6-mistral-7b, WizardLM-13B-V1.2, Llama-3.2-1B-instruct, Llama-2-7b-chat, CodeLlama-34b-Instruct (×2), Llama-2-7B (×2). (From my earlier notes, paper Table 5.)
- **Models used inside submitted routers (59 names, from all 36 prediction files; rows = question answers with a score):**
  - Many rows: qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 (47.7k rows, 73% right), deepseek-v4-flash (44.2k, 77%), gemini-3-flash-preview (28.7k, 80%), gemini-3.1-flash-lite (27.6k, 77%), deepseek-v3.2 (14.1k, 72%), deepseek-v4-pro (13.0k, 75%), Qwen3-Coder-Next (10.0k), grok-4-1-fast-reasoning (9.9k, 77%), gemini-3.7-flash (8.3k, 82%), gpt-oss-120b (8.1k, 70%), glm-5.3-flash (7.4k, 76%), agnes-2.0-flash (6.8k, 80%), gpt-5.6-luna (5.3k, 74%).
  - Frontier-ish: claude-opus-4-7 (4.4k rows, 79%), gemini-3.1-pro-preview (1.3k), claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-haiku-4-5, gemma-4-31b-it, Kimi-K2.6, MiniMax-M3, mimo-v2.5, glm-4.7.
  - Effort-tagged: deepseek-v4.1-flash@low (703 rows, 77%) vs @high (248, 69%); glm-5.3@high / @low (tiny).
  - Note: each router only answers with the model it picked. So per model you get a biased subset, not all 8,400. Only gemini-3-flash-preview, deepseek-v3.2 (and nearly qwen3-235b, deepseek-v4) cover all 8,400.
  - Accuracy here is the router's own run. The judge is RouterArena's scorer, not checked for every file.
- No GPT-6, Claude Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.x, Gemini 4 or DeepSeek V4 full (non-flash/pro) rows found.

## Metrics
- Accuracy, cost per 1k queries, optimality (selection / cost / accuracy vs oracle), robustness (same choice on noisy copy), latency.
- Arena score S = (1+β)·A·C / (β·A + C). C = log-normalised cost (c_min 0.0044, c_max 200). β = 0.1 (accuracy-heavy).

## Key findings
- Paper (12 routers): GPT-5's own router is most accurate (74.0%) but costs $14.02/1k. Azure Model Router 68.1% at $0.54. NotDiamond 68.0% at $9.34. CARROT 67.2% at $2.06. RouteLLM 47.0%. RouterDC 32.0%.
- All routers fall short of the oracle. Main reason: they do not drop to cheap models when cheap is enough.
- Hard questions: most routers < 10%. GPT-5 27.5%.
- Robustness is low for commercial and BERT-based routers.
- Live leaderboard (Nov 2026 README): Divyam 77.19 score / 80.83% / $0.66 per 1k; BizRouter 77.08 / 81.66% / $1.00; Sqwish 76.34 / 79.88% / $0.69; R2 Reasonometry 76.16 / 78.97% / $0.48.
- Paix2, R2-Router and AgentForge were pulled from the ranking pending an integrity review.

## For Yugos
- Overlap with Yugos list: MMLU-Pro (2,528), LiveCodeBench (385), AIME (39), MATH (55), GSM8K (24). Also medical (PubMedQA/MedMCQA, close to MedQA) and FinQA.
- Missing: GPQA, HLE, SimpleQA, BBEH, MuSR, ARC, Winogrande, HellaSwag, Arena-Hard, long context, all agentic (no SWE-bench, tau2, Terminal-Bench, BFCL).
- Model freshness: the HF data has no answers. But the router prediction files hold 2026 models (DeepSeek V4 flash/pro, Gemini 3.x, Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.6-luna). Still one step behind Yugos's frontier pool.
- Effort data: very little. A few `@low` / `@high` tags and some `thinking_config` fields.
- How to use:
  - Use as a ready test harness and difficulty labels (easy/medium/hard per question).
  - Mine `router_inference/predictions/*.json` as free per-question answers + accuracy + cost for 2026 models. Watch the selection bias.
  - Use the robustness split to check that a Yugos router is stable under typos.
  - Do not train on it if you want to submit to the leaderboard.

# Router benchmark step 5: SPROUT (CARROT paper) (2026-11-26)

- Who: Seamus Somerstep, Felipe Maia Polo, Allysson Flavio Melo de Oliveira, Prattyush Mangal, Mírian Silva, Onkar Bhardwaj, Mikhail Yurochkin, Subha Maity. IBM Research, MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab, U. Michigan, U. Waterloo, UFMG. Feb 2025 (v2 May 2025). arXiv preprint, no venue listed. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03261
- Data (2 HF sets, both under https://huggingface.co/CARROT-LLM-Routing):
  - `CARROT-LLM-Routing/SPROUT`: 13 models. 581 MB parquet: `data/train-0000{0,1,2}-of-00003.parquet` (~135 MB each), `validation` 87 MB, `test` 87 MB. 44,241 rows.
  - `CARROT-LLM-Routing/SPROUT-o3mini`: same 13 models **+ o3-mini** (14). 618 MB parquet. 43,288 rows (30,301 / 6,493 / 6,494). A few hundred questions fewer.
- Licence: **none stated** on either card. README body is empty.
- Columns: `key` (64-char hash), `dataset`, `dataset_level` (MATH level), `dataset_idx`, `prompt`, `golden_answer`, then one struct column per model: `response`, `num_input_tokens`, `num_output_tokens`, `score` (0–1), `judge_response`.
- How made: zero-shot, each model's own chat template. Tokens counted by each model's tokenizer. Judge = Llama-3.1-70B, MixEval-style, vs the gold answer. Cost = tokens × list price.

## Sub-benchmarks (6 sources, 44,241 prompts)
| Area | Benchmark | Train | Val | Test | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chat / instructions | OpenHermes (teknium) | 13,670 | 2,873 | 2,912 | 19,455 |
| Knowledge | MMLU-Pro | 8,264 | 1,750 | 1,772 | 11,786 |
| Math | MATH (all levels 1–5) | 6,857 | 1,565 | 1,462 | 9,884 |
| RAG | RAGBench (12 subsets: CovidQA, CUAD, DelucionQA, FinQA, EManual, ExpertQA, HotpotQA, MS MARCO, TechQA, TAT-QA, PubMedQA, HAGRID) | 1,269 | 284 | 274 | 1,827 |
| Reasoning | MuSR (murder mystery, object placement, team allocation) | 524 | 101 | 123 | 748 |
| Science | GPQA **extended** | 384 | 63 | 94 | 541 |
| **Total** | | **30,968** | **6,636** | **6,637** | **44,241** |

- Counts are from the HF dataset server (`dataset` column). Checked. They match my earlier notes.
- MATH labels: train has Level 5 2,066, L4 1,566, L3 1,484, L2 1,197, L1 543.
- GPQA here is `gpqa_extended`, not Diamond.

## Models (13 in SPROUT, 14 in SPROUT-o3mini)
- OpenAI: gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, o3-mini (o3mini set only)
- Anthropic (via AWS): claude-3-5-sonnet-v1
- Amazon: titan-text-premier-v1
- Meta (via IBM watsonx): llama-3.2-1b-instruct, llama-3.2-3b-instruct, llama-3.1-8b-instruct, llama-3.1-70b-instruct, llama-3.3-70b-instruct, llama-3-405b-instruct
- IBM: granite-3-2b-instruct, granite-3-8b-instruct (8k max tokens)
- Mistral: mixtral-8x7b-instruct-v01
- Prices ($/1M in/out, paper Table 2): o3-mini 1.1/4.4, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 3/15, GPT-4o 2.5/10, GPT-4o-mini 0.15/0.6, Titan 0.5/1.5, Llama 405B 3.5/3.5, Llama 70B 0.9/0.9, Mixtral 0.6/0.6, Llama 8B 0.2/0.2, Granite 8B 0.2/0.2, Granite 2B 0.1/0.1, Llama 1B/3B 0.06/0.06.
- The paper says both "14 models" and "M=15". It lists o3-mini twice. So 14 is the real count.

## Key findings
- CARROT (simple router: predict score + cost per model, pick the best trade-off) matches or beats GPT-4o at ~30% of GPT-4o's cost.
- It does not beat o3-mini's accuracy, but gets close for a fraction of the cost (no number given).
- On RouterBench, routing barely helps. On SPROUT it helps a lot. Reason: SPROUT has harder, more varied questions.
- On Open LLM Leaderboard v2 data, CARROT beats the best single model (Qwen2-72B) by a large margin.
- RouterArena (paper, step 4) later scored CARROT at 67.2% for $2.06/1k.

## For Yugos
- Overlap with Yugos list: MMLU-Pro (11.8k), MATH (9.9k with levels), MuSR (748), GPQA (extended, not Diamond). OpenHermes ≈ general chat.
- Missing: everything in code and agentic. No HLE, SimpleQA, AIME, LiveCodeBench, SWE-bench, tau2.
- Model freshness: early 2025 at best (o3-mini, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet). No GPT-5, let alone GPT-6 / Claude 5.x / Gemini 4 / DeepSeek V4.
- Effort data: none. o3-mini effort level is not stated. But per-question output tokens are stored, so you can see "how long each model talks".
- Judge-based scores (Llama-3.1-70B), not exact match. Expect some noise.
- How to use:
  - Best open source of chat + math questions with gold answers and train/val/test splits. Good as Yugos-style eval prompts.
  - Re-run the questions on today's models to make fresh labels.
  - MATH levels give a ready difficulty signal for "cheap model vs strong model" tests.
  - R2-Bench (step 6) re-uses the SPROUT train split with length budgets.

# Router benchmark step 6: R2-Bench / R2-Router (2026-11-26)

- Who: Jiaqi Xue, Qian Lou, Jiarong Xing, Heng Huang. UCF + Rice + U. Maryland (affiliations from a search summary (unverified)). Feb 2026 (v2 May 2026). ICML 2026. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02823
- Code: https://github.com/UCF-ML-Research/R2-Router (MIT). Ships 187 small Ridge-regression checkpoints (`.joblib`) for 11 models.
- Data (2 HF sets):
  - **R2-Bench (paper data):** https://huggingface.co/datasets/JiaqiXue/R2-Bench (MIT). ~25.3 GB of CSV. Path `data/<org>/<model>/<budget>_judge.csv`. 155 files.
  - **R2-Bench-RouterArena:** https://huggingface.co/datasets/JiaqiXue/R2-Bench-RouterArena (no licence; `LICENSE_NOTE.md` says upstream rights stay with original owners). `budget_sweep/<model>/budget_<N>.json` on RouterArena's 8,400 questions, plus pickles (`training_data.pkl`, embeddings) and `routerarena_meta/*.json`.
- CSV columns (README): `prompts_id`, `key`, `original_prompt`, `templated_prompt`, `golden_answer`, `response`, `actual_token_count`, `judge_raw`, `correctness_score`.
  - The first line of `GLM-4.6/100_judge.csv` ends at `judge_raw`. So the score may sit inside `judge_raw` JSON in some files. (unverified)
- RouterArena sweep JSON fields: `global index`, `prompt`, `for_optimality`, `generated_result` (answer, token_usage, provider), `accuracy`, `cost`. Checked.
- Size: 30,968 questions × 10 models × 15–16 budgets ≈ 4.95M judged answers (README).

## Sub-benchmarks (6 sources = SPROUT train split, 30,968 prompts)
| Area | Benchmark | Prompts |
|---|---|---|
| Chat / instructions | OpenHermes | 13,670 |
| Knowledge | MMLU-Pro | 8,264 |
| Math | MATH (levels 1–5) | 6,857 |
| RAG | RAGBench (12 subsets) | 1,269 |
| Reasoning | MuSR | 524 |
| Science | GPQA extended | 384 |
| **Total** | | **30,968** |

- The paper (App. B.1) says MATH 5,122 and MuSR 100 and gives no RAGBench count. Those are wrong or partial. 5,122 is only one of the two MATH labels in SPROUT.
- My counts = SPROUT train split (checked on HF). Same total, same 64-char `key` hash column. Exact prompt-by-prompt match not checked (unverified).
- Second set: RouterArena's 8,400 questions (step 4), swept at budgets 10, 20, 40, 80, 150, 200, 400, 800, 1,500, unlimited, plus a "concise" prompt.

## Models
- **R2-Bench HF data (10 models):**
  - Qwen: Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct, Qwen3-0.6B
  - Meta: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct
  - Z-AI: GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.6 (these two and Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B lack the 8,000 budget = 15 files)
- **Paper (says 15, names 11 in Table 6):** Qwen3-0.6B, Gemma-3-1B, Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Gemma-3-4B-it, Mistral-7B-v0.2, Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.6, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct.
  - Gemma-3-1B, Gemma-3-4B and Mistral-7B are in the paper but have no folder in the HF data. Qwen3-Next-80B and Qwen3-30B are in the HF data but not in Table 6.
  - Code router pool (11) = Table 6 list with gemma-3-270m-it added (no GLM-4.6).
- **RouterArena sweep (15 folders):**
  - Full budget sweep: Qwen3-235B-2507, Qwen3-30B-A3B, Qwen3-Next-80B, Qwen3-Coder-Next, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, Ministral-3 3B / 8B / 14B (2512), Gemma-3n-E4B (no concise).
  - "Concise" prompt only: Gemini-3-Pro-preview, Gemini-2.5-Flash, GLM-5, GPT-5.2, GPT-4o, Claude-3-Haiku.
  - `model_cost.json` also lists Kimi-K2.5 (no sweep folder).

## How the budget works
- Budgets in HF data: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 80, 100, 150, 200, 300, 500, 800, 1,200, 2,000, 4,000, 8,000.
- Paper says 16 levels where the last is "default" (no instruction, 4,000-token cap). HF uses 8,000 instead. Small mismatch.
- Budget is given in the prompt, then answers are cut off.
  - Seen in the CSV: "You have a strict budget of 100 words. You must answer at most 100 words!" So the prompt says **words**, while files are named by tokens.
- Compliance: big models stay within 1.1× budget 82% of the time at 10 tokens, 97% at ≥100. Models under 4B: only 3–21% at 10 tokens.
- Judge: "Qwen3-80B-Instruct" (likely Qwen3-Next-80B (unverified)). Scores 0–1. Pearson 0.82 vs humans on 500 answers.

## Key findings
- A model's quality is not fixed. It changes with answer length. So route on (model, budget), not model only.
- A strong model with a short budget often beats a weak model with a long budget at the same cost.
- R2-Router: ~0.8 average quality at ~0.5×10⁻³ $/query. Other routers need 4–5× the cost for that.
- Oracle on SPROUT (3 models): adding budget choice lifts AUDC 0.85 → 0.98 and peak quality 0.90 → 0.98.
- New-model test: AUDC 0.623 vs UniRoute 0.590. Out-of-domain (MMLU-Pro STEM → non-STEM): 0.71 vs CARROT 0.67.
- Only 6–8 budget "anchors" are needed to predict the full quality-vs-length curve.
- RouterArena: claimed #1 at acceptance. Now **pulled from the RouterArena ranking pending an integrity review** (RouterArena README, Nov 2026).

## For Yugos
- Overlap with Yugos list: MMLU-Pro, MATH, MuSR, GPQA (extended, not Diamond). Plus RouterArena's MMLU-Pro / LiveCodeBench / AIME / MATH / GSM8K in the sweep set.
- Missing: code (except LiveCodeBench in sweep), all agentic, HLE, SimpleQA, AIME (main set).
- Model freshness: open models from 2024–2025. Sweep set adds GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-Pro, GLM-5 but only one "concise" setting. No GPT-6 / Claude 5.x / Gemini 4 / DeepSeek V4.
- Effort data: **the best public data on "how much to think"**, but it is answer-length budget via prompt, not the provider's reasoning-effort knob. Treat it as a proxy.
- How to use:
  - Learn the shape of the quality-vs-length curve per question type (e.g. MMLU-Pro saturates early, MATH needs long answers).
  - Use the "anchors" idea: test Yugos models at 3–4 effort levels, interpolate the rest.
  - Copy the joint (model, budget) router design for Yugos's (provider, model, effort) choice.
  - Be careful: 25 GB of CSV; pickles in the RouterArena set (sandbox only); leaderboard integrity flag.

# Router benchmark step 7: TwinRouterBench (2026-11-26)

- Who: 18 authors. Lead lab Gradient (corresponding author Tianyu Shi), with Soochow Univ., Amazon, Rice, CMU, HKUST, UC Berkeley and others. Code under GitHub org CommonstackAI. First posted 14 May 2026; latest version v5 on 24 Oct 2026. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18859
  - Venue: arXiv lists none. The "NeurIPS 2026" label in my earlier table is (unverified).
- Code: https://github.com/CommonstackAI/TwinRouterBench (Apache-2.0).
- Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Amorph/TwinRouterBench (Apache-2.0, ~18 MB, not gated).
  - `data/train.parquet`: 970 rows, 1.3 MB.
  - `question_bank.jsonl`: the same 970 raw records, 17 MB.
  - `manifest.json`: source counts and schema.
  - GitHub also has `data/dynamic/` with `model_pool.json`, `model_pricing.json`, `tier_to_model.json`, `ttl_policy.json`, `sr_knn_to_pool.json`, and `dynamic_heldout100_ids.txt` (the 100 leaderboard tasks).
- Columns: `id, benchmark, scenario, instance_id, step_index, total_steps, messages` (JSON string = the conversation so far), `functions` (tool schemas as JSON), `target_tier` (low / mid / mid_high / high), `target_tier_id` (0–3), plus `benchmark_display, benchmark_subset, benchmark_version, pipeline_stage, collector, collected_at, notes`.
- Size: 970 labelled agent steps from 520 tasks.
  - It is not a question × model table. Each row stores one label: the cheapest tier that still lets the whole task pass.
  - The rows hold no model IDs and no model answers.
- Two tracks:
  - Static: score the router's tier choice offline, with no LLM judge.
  - Dynamic: run the router live inside a SWE-bench agent, then count real cost and tasks solved.

## Sub-benchmarks (5 workloads)
| Area | Benchmark | Tasks | Labelled steps (rows) | Gold tier low / mid / mid_high / high |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agentic (code) | SWE-bench Verified (40-task subset) | 40 | 336 | 94 / 33 / 41 / 168 |
| Agentic (tools) | BFCL v4 (multi-turn 148, single-turn 100) | 130 | 248 | 239 / 8 / 1 / 0 |
| Agentic (general) | PinchBench (12 of its tasks) | 12 | 48 | 41 / 3 / 3 / 1 |
| Chat / RAG | mtRAG (multi-turn RAG) | 193 | 193 | 183 / 8 / 1 / 1 |
| Chat / summary | QMSum (meeting summaries) | 145 | 145 | 132 / 10 / 3 / 0 |
| **Total** | | **520** | **970** | **689 / 62 / 49 / 170** |
| Live (dynamic track) | SWE-bench Verified held-out (18 Astropy + 82 Django) | 100 | — | — |

- Row counts and tier counts come from the HF stats and `manifest.json`. Task counts come from the paper.
- BFCL subsets: multi_turn_base 74, multi_turn_long_context 74, parallel_multiple 33, live_multiple 25, live_parallel_multiple 22, multiple 11, live_irrelevance 9.
- The paper calls PinchBench a 23-task suite, but the dataset card says 53 tasks. Either way, only 12 tasks are used.

## Models (11 in 4 tiers, static track)
- High: claude-opus-4.6, gpt-5.4
- Mid-high: claude-haiku-4.5, gemini-3-flash-preview, qwen3.5-397b-a17b
- Mid: minimax-m2.5, qwen3.5-27b, qwen3-coder
- Low: deepseek-v3.2, glm-4.5-air, qwen3.5-9b
- Dynamic pool (4 models; $ per 1M tokens in / out):
  - claude-opus-4.6: 5.00 / 25.00
  - gemini-3-flash-preview: 0.50 / 3.00
  - minimax-m2.7: 0.30 / 1.20
  - deepseek-v3.2: 0.252 / 0.378
- Router embedder (not in the pool): Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B.

## Key findings
- Most steps need only the cheap tier: 71% of steps are "low".
- Steps that need a strong model are almost all in SWE (168 of 170 "high" steps).
- From my earlier notes, the share of steps needing a strong model:
  - test/debug 72%
  - read 56%
  - patch 50%
  - tool calls under 1%
- Live test on 100 SWE tasks:
  - Trained UncommonRoute solved 75 for $25.66.
  - Opus 4.6 alone solved 74 for $54.73.
  - So the router was 53% cheaper.
- Rule-based routers (ClawRouter, UncommonRoute rules) failed 38–39 of the 40 SWE trajectories in the static test. Getting even one step wrong kills the whole task.
- Opus 4.6 used as a router picked "high" for only 7 of 147 truly-high SWE steps.
- The paper does not use reasoning effort levels.

## For Yugos
- Overlap: SWE-bench Verified and BFCL are both on the Yugos list. mtRAG, QMSum and PinchBench are not. There is no tau2 and no Terminal-Bench.
- Models are early-2026 (Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4). None are GPT-6, Opus 5.5 or Gemini 4. The tier idea still carries over.
- No effort data: labels are tiers, not effort levels.
- Agentic coverage is good. This is the only set with labels per agent step.
- How to use it:
  - Train a "how hard is this step" classifier on the SWE and BFCL rows.
  - Map its 4 tiers onto the Yugos price ladder, e.g. low = DeepSeek V4 and high = Opus 5.5 or GPT-6.
  - Lesson for tau2: cheap models handle most tool-call steps. Spend on the hard steps only.
- Gap: the rows store labels only, with no per-model right/wrong answers. You can't swap in new models without re-running the whole thing.

# Router benchmark step 8: HM-Router (2026-11-26)

- Who: Imperial College London (Hao Mark Chen, Dimitris Anastasiou, Wayne Luk, Hongxiang Fan), Samsung (Royson Lee), Institute of Science Tokyo (Yasuyuki Okoshi). Posted 26 Sep 2026. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32213 (paper text is CC BY 4.0).
- Data: https://github.com/hmarkc/HM-Router, folder `data/` (one commit, 7 stars).
  - `hm_router_bench.csv`: 3.1 MB, 39,626 rows.
    - Columns: `benchmark, query_id, model, harness, scaffold, acc`.
    - `acc` is between 0 and 1: either the success rate over several runs, or a rubric score on workspace_bench_lite.
    - Most rows are 0 or 1: 18,501 zeros and 14,050 ones.
  - `queries.csv`: 1.7 MB, 1,648 rows. Columns: `benchmark, query_id, query` (the task text).
- Licence: none. The repo has no LICENSE file, and the GitHub API returns `license: null`. So reuse rights are unclear.
- Size: 1,648 tasks across 12 agent benchmarks.
  - 293 routes. A route is one (model, harness) pair inside one benchmark.
  - There are 264 distinct pairs across all benchmarks.
  - Every route covers every task of its benchmark, so each benchmark is a full table.
- Main idea: pick the model and the agent harness together, e.g. Claude Code vs Codex vs OpenHands.
- Result source: the paper does not say where the results come from. They look like public leaderboard runs (HAL, tbench, SWE-bench) (unverified).

## Sub-benchmarks (12)
| Area | Benchmark | Tasks | Routes (model × harness) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agentic (code) | SWE-bench Verified | 500 | 24 |
| Agentic (web) | Online-Mind2Web | 300 | 20 |
| Agentic (assistant) | GAIA | 165 | 25 |
| Agentic (harness) | harness_bench | 106 | 45 |
| Agentic (workspace) | workspace_bench_lite | 100 | 27 |
| Agentic (terminal) | Terminal-Bench 2.1 | 89 | 15 |
| Agentic (skills) | SkillsBench | 87 | 25 |
| Agentic (tools) | tau-bench airline (v1, HAL harnesses) | 50 | 18 |
| Agentic (science) | CORE-Bench Hard | 45 | 39 |
| Agentic (science) | CORE-Bench v1.1 | 39 | 13 |
| Code (science) | ScienceAgentBench | 102 | 17 |
| Code (science) | SciCode | 65 | 25 |
| **Total** | | **1,648** | **293** |

All counts were checked by me in `hm_router_bench.csv`.

## Models (73 names ≈ 67 models)
Some models appear under 2 spellings, e.g. gpt-5-4 / gpt-5.4 and glm-5-1 / glm-5.1.
- Anthropic: claude-fable-5, claude-opus-3/4/4-1/4-5/4-6/4-7/4-8, claude-sonnet-3-5/3-7/3-7:thinking/4/4-5/4-6/5, claude-haiku-3-5/4-5
- OpenAI: gpt-4o, gpt-4-1, gpt-4-1106-preview, gpt-5, gpt-5-1, gpt-5-2, gpt-5.2-codex, gpt-5-3-codex, gpt-5-4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5-5, gpt-5-6-luna, gpt-5-6-terra, gpt-oss-120b, o3, o3-mini, o4-mini
- Google: gemini-2-0-flash, gemini-2-5-pro-preview-03-25, gemini-3-pro-preview, gemini-3-flash, gemini-3-1-pro (+ preview), gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3.5-flash
- DeepSeek: deepseek-v3, v3-0324, v3-1, r1, r1-0528, deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v4-pro
- Others: glm-4-5/4-6/5-1, kimi-k2 (instruct, 0711-preview, 2.5, k2.6), minimax-m2.7, minimax-m3, qwen-3.6-plus, qwen-3-coder-30b/480b, grok-4.3, hy3, devstral-small-2505/2507, skywork-swe-32b, swe-agent-lm-32b
- Harnesses: 27 names (25 after merging duplicates), e.g.:
  - general coding: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, OpenHands, SWE-agent, Terminus 2
  - HAL agents: HAL Generalist, Taubench ToolCalling
  - others: Browser-Use, SeeAct, HF Open Deep Research, OpenClaw, Hermes, nanobot, …

### Where the newest models are
- The newest models appear in only 1–2 benchmarks each:
  - Terminal-Bench 2.1 only: claude-fable-5, claude-sonnet-5, gpt-5-6-luna, gpt-5-6-terra, gpt-5-5
  - Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SkillsBench: claude-opus-4-8
  - SkillsBench (some also workspace_bench_lite or harness_bench): deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v4-pro, gemini-3.5-flash, grok-4.3, minimax-m3, kimi-k2.6, glm-5.1, gpt-5.5
- tau-bench airline has only older models: gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, gpt-5, o3, o4-mini, claude-sonnet-3.5/3.7, opus-4/4.1, gemini-2.0-flash, deepseek-v3, deepseek-r1.
  - Best route there: o3 + Taubench ToolCalling = 0.54.
- Best routes on Terminal-Bench 2.1:
  - claude-fable-5 + Claude Code 0.838
  - gpt-5-5 + Codex 0.831
  - claude-fable-5 + Terminus 2 0.804
  - claude-opus-4-8 + Claude Code 0.789

## Key findings
- Mean routing accuracy over 12 benchmarks, normalised to the oracle:
  - HM-Router 73.9%
  - IRT 66.7%
  - Avengers 66.6%
  - EmbedLLM 65.5%
  - Random 49.6%
- So HM-Router is 7.3 points above the best learned baseline.
- The harness matters as much as the model. The same model can score very differently in different harnesses.
- Sharing model and harness "embeddings" lets the router guess pairs it never saw. With 90% of routes hidden, this gave +15.8 points.
- Cost subset (6 benchmarks, $0.75–$10 per task budgets): HM-Router leads at every budget. At $2 per task it scores 69.2% vs 60.7%.
- Split: 70/30 per benchmark, 5 seeds.
- There is no reasoning-effort data. The only effort-like name is `claude-3-7-sonnet:thinking`.

## For Yugos
- Overlap with the Yugos list:
  - SWE-bench Verified (500)
  - Terminal-Bench (2.1, 89)
  - tau airline, but this is tau-bench v1 (50), not tau2
  - no BFCL, no tau2 banking, retail or telecom
- Model freshness: this is the freshest set so far, with Fable 5, Opus 4.8, GPT-5.6 luna/terra and DeepSeek V4. But only Terminal-Bench and SkillsBench have them. No GPT-6, Opus 5.5 or Gemini 4.
- No effort data. There is a harness dimension, which Yugos doesn't have.
- Agentic coverage: all 12 benchmarks are agentic or code.
- How to use it:
  - Use Terminal-Bench 2.1 rows for a frontier pecking order on terminal tasks, e.g. Fable 5 ≈ GPT-5.5 > Opus 4.8.
  - Use SWE-bench rows to learn which task types need a strong model.
  - Take the method idea: separate embeddings for "model" and "setting". The setting could be effort level instead of harness.
- Gaps:
  - No licence.
  - No per-task cost in the CSV. Cost is only in the paper's subset.
  - The table is sparse: new models are missing from most benchmarks.

# Router benchmark step 9: Nine-by-30k / Routing Plateau (2026-11-26)

- Who: Rice University (Yifan Lu, Qiyue Zhang, Shenrun Zhang, Zhibo Yu, Hanjie Chen, Jiarong Xing) and Amazon (Zhuang Wang). This is the same Rice group behind RouterArena.
  - v1 posted 27 May 2026, v2 on 28 Sep 2026. arXiv lists no venue.
  - Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07587 ("The Routing Plateau: Understanding the Accuracy Limits of LLM Routers"; paper text is CC BY 4.0)
- Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/RouteWorks/Nine-by-30k, uploaded 11 Sep 2026.
  - The paper itself gives no link. I found the dataset under the RouteWorks HF org.
  - 10 parquet shards, 2.7 GB in total. One shard alone is 2.58 GB.
  - No licence on the card. The README only lists the schema.
- Columns: `Sub-category, Category` (Dewey-style subject labels), `Dataset name, Global Index, Context, Question, Options, Answer, Metadata`.
  - **There are no model answers or scores in the HF data.** It holds the questions only.
  - The 9-model 0–1 labels and costs are described in the paper but not published. I found them in no HF or GitHub location.
- Size:
  - HF data: 310,371 questions. This is the "Nine-by-300k" pool: 302,371 train + 3,000 val + 5,000 test.
  - Nine-by-30k: a 10% sample with 31,027 prompts (23,027 train, 3,000 val, 5,000 test). The val and test splits are the same as in the 300k set.
  - The paper says 2.8M question × model labels in total.
- Scoring:
  - Each (question, model) pair gets a score from 0 to 1.
  - Rules first: letter match, exact match or F1, math equivalence, unit tests for code, METEOR for NarrativeQA.
  - A gpt-4o-mini judge is used only for QANTA, WebQuestions and ChemistryQA, and only when the rules fail.
  - Costs come from OpenRouter token counts × list prices.
  - Decoding used provider defaults. No reasoning or effort setting is reported.

## Sub-benchmarks (57 datasets in 6 groups; Nine-by-30k counts from paper Table 8)
| Area | Benchmark(s) | Prompts (30k) |
|---|---|---|
| Multiple choice (21) | MMLU 1,323 · ETHICS 1,127 · MMLU-Pro 1,100 · HellaSwag 1,024 · MedMCQA 626 · CaseHOLD 536 · BoolQ 341 · ARC-Easy 244 · MedQA 143 · CommonsenseQA 123 · Winogrande 121 · ARC-Challenge 114 · SciQ 107 · QASC 98 · TruthfulQA 82 · ArcMMLU 69 · FinQA 69 · OpenBookQA 55 · GPQA 52 · BioASQ 38 · MusicTheoryBench 33 | 7,425 |
| Math (6) | MathQA 282 · AsDiv 246 · GSM8K 148 · MATH 51 · AQuA-RAT 28 · SVAMP 28 | 783 |
| Code (3) | MBPP 52 · LiveCodeBench 50 · HumanEval 19 | 121 |
| Reading / open QA (18) | SearchQA 4,404 · MLQA 4,157 · Social IQa 3,322 · XQuAD 1,458 · SQuAD 1,075 · NarrativeQA 1,005 · MS MARCO 870 · HotpotQA 773 · CoQA 726 · QuAC 642 · WikiHop 525 · TyDi QA 494 · NewsQA 369 · NQ-Open 300 · WebQuestions 202 · Qanta 197 · PANDAX-patent-QA 181 (internal) · ChemistryQA 50 | 20,750 |
| SuperGLUE-style (7) | ClozeTest 935 · RC 463 · QA 319 · WiC 69 · Entailment 25 · WSC 14 · CausalReasoning 8 | 1,833 |
| Domain (2) | LSAT-AR 102 · ChessInstruct 13 | 115 |
| **Total** | | **31,027** |

- Counts in the HF 310k pool (from HF stats), for the Yugos-relevant sets:
  - Knowledge: MMLU 13,766; MMLU-Pro at least 11,108 (13 subject splits in the stats I saw; the full MMLU-Pro has 12,032); HellaSwag 10,042; Winogrande 1,267; ARC-Challenge 1,172; ARC-Easy 2,376; MedQA 1,273; GPQA 546; TruthfulQA 817
  - Math: GSM8K 1,319; MathQA 2,983
  - Code: LiveCodeBench 511; MBPP 499; HumanEval 164
- The table lists 57 datasets. The paper says 56 are public and 1 (PANDAX patent QA) is internal, although the internal split still appears on HF (1,810 rows).

## Models (9, via OpenRouter)
- Chinese open: deepseek-v3.2, qwen3-235b-a22b-2507, qwen3-coder-next, glm-4.5-air, minimax-m2.5, mimo-v2-flash
- Other open: llama-3.3-70b-instruct, gemma-3n-e4b-it
- API: grok-4.1-fast

## Key findings
- They tested 21 routers on 5 benchmarks: RouterBench, Nine-by-30k, EmbedLLM, R2-Bench and SPROUT/CARROT.
- **The "routing plateau":**
  - The top 5 routers differ by only 0.22 points on average.
  - On RouterBench, the top 15 are within 0.23 points.
  - Simple kNN (76.95% average) is about as good as the best (Zooter, 77.01%).
- The best router is still 10.6–29.4 points below the oracle. The oracle scores 0.827 on Nine-by-30k.
- The reason: routers learn "which model is best on average", not "which model is best for this exact question".
- Hard questions cause 53–81% of the gap to the oracle.
- 10× more data plus bigger encoders and fine-tuning gave only +1.24 points on average. Routers stayed about 13 points below the oracle.
- The authors suggest using more than the question text, e.g. a model's partial answer, to break the plateau.

## For Yugos
- Overlap with the Yugos list:
  - MMLU-Pro, GPQA, MedQA, ARC challenge/easy, Winogrande, HellaSwag, GSM8K, MATH, LiveCodeBench, HumanEval, MBPP
  - no agentic, no BBEH, no HLE, no AIME
- Model freshness: low. These are mid-tier open models from late 2025 / early 2026. No GPT-6, Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 or DeepSeek V4.
- No effort data. No agentic tasks.
- How to use it:
  - Main value is the lesson: don't expect a smarter text-only router to beat kNN by much. Gains come from new signals, e.g. effort, a cheap first try, or self-check.
  - The 310k question pool is a big, clean, labelled-by-subject question bank. Use it to make your own practice sets for Yugos chat/QA, then label them with your own model + effort runs.
- Gaps:
  - Per-model labels are not public (only questions on HF).
  - No licence for the data.
  - The source datasets keep their own licences.

# Router benchmark step 10: xRouteBench / LLMRouter (2026-11-26)

- Who: UIUC (Jiaxuan You's lab; first author Tao Feng), with Purdue, UMD, NTU and UIC. This is the same group as GraphRouter and FusionBench.
  - Posted 7 Aug 2026. arXiv lists no venue.
  - Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06867 ("LLMRouter: Unified Infrastructure for Developing, Evaluating, and Deploying LLM Routers")
- Code: https://github.com/ulab-uiuc/LLMRouter (MIT licence). It has about 16–19 routers: 13 single-round, 1 multi-round, 1 multimodal, 2 personalised, 2 "agentic".
- Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ulab-ai/xRouteBench, last updated 15 Aug 2026.
  - Format: parquet, one folder per scenario, with `train.parquet` and `test.parquet`.
  - No licence on the dataset card. The MIT licence covers the code only.
- Columns: one row = one (question, model) pair.
  - Question: `task_name, query, ground_truth, metric, choices, task_id`
  - Model run: `model_name, response, token_num, input_tokens, output_tokens, response_time` (latency in seconds), `performance` (0–1), `embedding_id`
  - The full model answer text is stored.
- Extra configs:
  - `*_queries`: questions only, with train / valid / test splits, so you can run your own models.
  - `llm_candidates`: the 18 models with prices. Columns: `model_name, size, input_price_per_1m, output_price_per_1m, service, api_model_id, description`.
  - Cost per row = input_tokens × input price + output_tokens × output price.
- Size:
  - 8 scenarios.
  - 4,767 test questions (paper).

## Models (18 cheap models, via Together AI / NVIDIA NIM; $ per 1M tokens in / out)
- Small (7–24B):
  - qwen2.5-7b-instruct 0.2/0.2
  - qwen2.5-7b-instruct-turbo 0.3/0.3

  - gemma-2-9b-it 0.1/0.1

- Mid (47–120B):
  - mixtral-8x7b-instruct 0.6/0.6

## Key findings
- Learned routers beat the best single fixed model by 14.6% (relative, per the abstract).
  - Table 2 average: GraphRouter 45.46 vs largest model 38.72.
- Best router on the generic set: RouterDC, 80.56 vs 70.29 for the largest model.
- The top routers are close together: GraphRouter 45.46, SVMRouter 45.10, EloRouter 44.68.
- Light routers do relatively better when the budget is tight.
- Routing that knows the user (GMTRouter) helps personalised chat: 68.8% judge accuracy.

## For Yugos
- Overlap with the Yugos list:

  - Arena-style chat is loosely similar to Arena-Hard
  - no agentic sets, no tau2, no SWE-bench
- Model freshness: low. These are cheap open models (2024 – early 2026). Only gpt-oss and deepseek-v3.1 are near what Yugos might use as a cheap tier.
- No effort data.
- No agentic coverage, despite "agentic routers" in the code.
- How to use it:
  - Good clean data with token counts, latency and full answers. Use it to test cost-aware routing math, e.g. reward = quality − β × cost.
  - The LLMRouter toolkit (MIT) is a ready-made harness to plug in Yugos's own (question, model+effort) table and compare 16+ router types quickly.
  - The `*_queries` configs give clean question lists to re-run on frontier models.
- Gaps:
  - No dataset licence.
  - The MMLU-Pro train split is tiny (63).
  - Some test sets have only 13–50 items, so per-dataset scores are noisy.

# Router benchmark step 11: FusionBench / LLMFusionBench (2026-11-26)

- Who: UIUC (Tao Feng, Pengrui Han, Jiaxuan You) and NVIDIA (Patwary, Shoeybi, Catanzaro), plus NTU and Meta. This is the same lab as xRouteBench and GraphRouter.
  - v1 posted 14 Jul 2025 as "Fusing LLM Capabilities with Routing Data". v3 on 1 Jul 2026.
  - Published in TMLR 2026.
  - Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.10540 ("FusionFactory: Fusing LLM Capabilities with Multi-LLM Log Data")
- Code: https://github.com/ulab-uiuc/FusionFactory. Project page: https://ulab-uiuc.github.io/FusionFactory.
  - The GitHub API shows no licence. A README snippet says MIT (unverified).
- Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ulab-ai/FusionBench (~372 MB, last updated 30 Jun 2025). No licence on the card.
  - `train/`: 255,920 rows, 63 MB.
  - `partial_test/`: 27,760 rows. Both have model answers.
  - `full_test/`: 69,278 questions with no model answers.
  - `thought_template_{8b,70b}_{small,full}/`: 5.6k–6.7k rows of reasoning templates.
  - Also small configs: `thought_templates` (45 rows) and `sample_queries` (36 rows).
  - All are parquet.
- Columns (train / partial_test):
  - Question: `task_name, task_id, task_description, query, ground_truth, metric`
  - Model and price: `llm, llm_description, input_price, output_price`
  - Run: `input_tokens_num, output_tokens_num, response, cost, performance` (0–1), `llm_judge` (0–1 judge score)
- Size:
  - 7,092 questions with answers from 40 "model modes": 20 models × 2 modes (direct and `_think`). So 283,680 rows.
  - Tokens were counted with the GPT-2 tokenizer and priced with Together AI prices.
- **Two modes per model:**
  - "direct" = answer straight away.
  - `_think` = chain-of-thought prompt. For most models this is prompted CoT, not a native thinking mode.
  - This is the closest thing to "effort" data in this batch.

## Sub-benchmarks (14 tasks, 6 domains)
| Area | Benchmark | Train | Partial test | With answers | Full test (no answers) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Math | GSM8K | 500 | 50 | 550 | 1,319 |
| Math | MATH | 504 | 56 | 560 | 5,000 |
| Code | MBPP | 374 | 50 | 424 | 500 |
| Code | HumanEval | 120 | 44 | 164 | 44 |
| Commonsense | CommonsenseQA | 500 | 50 | 550 | 1,221 |
| Commonsense | ARC-Challenge | 500 | 50 | 550 | 1,172 |
| Commonsense | HellaSwag | 500 | 50 | 550 | 10,042 |
| Commonsense | OpenBookQA | 500 | 50 | 550 | 500 |
| World knowledge | NaturalQuestions | 500 | 50 | 550 | 3,610 |
| World knowledge | TriviaQA | 500 | 50 | 550 | 17,944 |
| Reading | SQuAD | 500 | 50 | 550 | 10,570 |
| Reading | BoolQ | 500 | 50 | 550 | 3,270 |
| "Popular" | MMLU | 500 | 50 | 550 | 14,042 |
| "Popular" | GPQA | 400 | 44 | 444 | 44 |
| **Total** | | **6,398** | **694** | **7,092** | **69,278** |

- I checked all counts in the HF stats (rows ÷ 40 model modes).
- My earlier note said 7,082. The checked number is 7,092.
- The abstract says "five domains", but the body and the HF `task_category` use 6.

## Models (20 open, 8B–671B; each in direct + `_think` mode)
- Small (7–12B): qwen2-7b-instruct, qwen2.5-7b-instruct, mistral-7b-instruct-v0.3, gemma-7b, codegemma-7b, gemma-2-9b-it, llama-3.1-8b-instruct, granite-3.0-8b-instruct, llama3-chatqa-1.5-8b, mistral-nemo-12b-instruct
- Medium (34–70B): llama-3.3-nemotron-super-49b-v1, granite-34b-code-instruct, llama-3.1-nemotron-51b-instruct, llama3-chatqa-1.5-70b, llama-3.1-70b-instruct, llama3-70b-instruct, mixtral-8x7b-instruct-v0.1
- Large (122–671B): palmyra-creative-122b, mixtral-8x22b-instruct-v0.1, deepseek-r1
- No closed API models.

## Key findings
- From the paper:
  - Query-level routing (GraphRouter): 0.602 score at cost 0.018, vs the best single model at 0.546 and cost 0.185. That's about 10× cheaper and better.
  - Thought-level fusion (reusing reasoning templates) has the best overall average: 0.615 vs 0.600 for the best single model.
  - Model-level fusion (distilling into one model) gives almost nothing (+0.01 to +0.02).
  - Math and world-knowledge gain the least, at most about 2 points.
- My check of direct vs think in `train` (6,398 questions):
  - Overall: think 0.586 vs direct 0.554. Think uses about 1.75× more output tokens (203 vs 116).
  - Think helps most on: ARC-C (+0.11), OpenBookQA (+0.09), HellaSwag (+0.08), CommonsenseQA (+0.06), MATH (+0.035), GSM8K (+0.024).
  - Think does not help, or slightly hurts, on: BoolQ (−0.03), MBPP (−0.02), HumanEval (−0.01), TriviaQA and NaturalQuestions (±0). GPQA is near zero for everyone (0.14 vs 0.15).
  - By model:
    - Big gains for weak chat models, e.g. llama3-chatqa-70b 0.28 → 0.48.
    - Gains for qwen2.5-7b, e.g. 0.59 → 0.65.
    - Small losses for code models, e.g. granite-34b-code 0.43 → 0.38, codegemma 0.43 → 0.39.
    - No change for deepseek-r1 (0.674 vs 0.676), which already reasons.

## For Yugos
- Overlap with the Yugos list:
  - GSM8K, MATH, MBPP, HumanEval, ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, GPQA (but small, and not the Diamond split)
  - MMLU (Yugos uses MMLU-Pro)
  - no agentic tasks
- Model freshness: very low. These are 2024-era open models, with DeepSeek-R1 the newest. No GPT-6, Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 or DeepSeek V4.
- Effort data: yes, but crude. There are two levels: direct vs CoT prompt. It is the only set in this batch with a paired "think more vs less" label on the same questions.
- How to use it:
  - Learn an "is extra thinking worth it" signal per question type. Lesson: thinking helps commonsense and math, not recall (TriviaQA) or code.
  - Treat that as a prior for Yugos effort choice, e.g. low effort for fact recall and higher effort for math.
  - The 69k `full_test` questions can be re-run on frontier models.
- Gaps:
  - No dataset licence.
  - Old models.
  - CoT prompting is not the same as real reasoning-effort settings (low / medium / high) on GPT-6 or Claude 5.x.
  - The GPQA and HumanEval test parts are tiny (44).

# Router benchmark step 12: EmbedLLM (2026-11-26)

- Who: UC Berkeley (Richard Zhuang, Tianhao Wu, Zhaojin Wen, Andrew Li, Jiantao Jiao, Kannan Ramchandran), Oct 2024. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.02223 (arXiv only; ICLR 2025 spotlight (unverified)). Code: https://github.com/richardzhuang0412/EmbedLLM
- Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/RZ412/EmbedLLM (~34 GB). Licence: Apache-2.0 (HF card).
  - Main files: `train.csv` 2.70 GB, `val.csv` 273 MB, `test.csv` 282 MB, `question_order.csv` 19.8 MB, `model_order.csv` 3.9 KB.
  - Also big `.pth` tensors (`train_x.pth` 20.4 GB, `val_x.pth`/`test_x.pth` 2.1 GB each, `question_embeddings.pth` 110 MB, `optimal_mf_model_embeddings.pth`). These are PyTorch pickles. Do not load them; use the CSVs.
  - `scalability/new_train_subset_{10,15,20,25}k.csv` (0.9–2.3 GB) = smaller train sets. They have an extra `Unnamed: 0` column, which breaks the HF viewer.
- Columns (CSV, one row = question × model): `prompt_id`, `model_id`, `category_id`, `label` (1 = right, 0 = wrong), `prompt`, `model_name`, `category`.
- Size: 112 models × ~36k questions ≈ 4.0M right/wrong labels.
  - Paper says 36,054 questions. My earlier HF count: 35,967. `question_order.csv` parses to 35,673 rows (my parse, 2026-11-26). Small gaps are probably dedup or parsing (unverified).
  - Split: random 80/10/10 by question (~29k train / ~3.6k val / ~3.6k test).
- Labels come from lm-evaluation-harness. Only right/wrong. No answer text, no cost, no tokens, no latency.

## Sub-benchmarks (10)
| Area | Benchmark | Prompts (HF data) |

| Knowledge | MMLU (57 subjects) | 14,015 |
| Science | GPQA (main + extended + diamond, each in several prompt formats) | 5,960 |
| Medicine | MedMCQA | 4,183 |

| Math | ASDiv | 2,304 |
| Math | GSM8K | 1,319 |
| **Total** | | **35,967** |

- Code: CodeLlama-7b-hf, CodeLlama-13b/34b-Instruct, CodeLlama-70B-Instruct-AWQ, octocoder, openbuddy-codellama2-34b
- Math: MetaMath-Mistral-7B, MetaMath-Llemma-7B, llemma_7b, llemma_34b, WizardLM-Math-70B, deepseek-math-7b, zephyr-beta-math, llama2-13b-math1.2
- Medical / science: BioMistral-7B (+DARE), BioMedGPT-LM-7B, medicine-LLM / medicine-LLM-13B / medicine-chat, palmyra-med-20b, vicuna-7B-physics/chemical, Llama-2-7B-physics, SciPhi-Mistral-7B-32k
- Older chat: vicuna 7B/13B/33B, koala-13B, falcon-40b-instruct, mpt-7b-chat, mpt-30b-instruct, dolly-v2-12b, stablelm-tuned-alpha-7b, pythia-12b, oasst-sft-4-pythia-12b, gpt4all-13b-snoozy, baize-v2-13b, bloom-7b1, tulu-30B, tulu-2-dpo-70b, WizardLM-70B
- Community 7B–72B merges: Starling-LM-7B alpha/beta, openchat_3.5/0106, zephyr-7b-beta, SOLAR-10.7B-Instruct, Nous-Hermes-13b, Nous-Hermes-2-Yi-34B, SUS-Chat-34B, Luminex-34B v0.1/v0.2, AlphaMonarch-7B, alpaca-dragon-72b, and ~20 more
- No API models (no GPT, Claude, Gemini).

## Key findings
- A matrix-factorization (MF) model learns one vector per LLM. It predicts right/wrong for a model on a new question: 0.741 accuracy vs 0.715 for KNN (full train set).
- The MF router beats "always pick the single best model" overall. It is close to the best model on each benchmark.
- It is fast: ~750 routing choices per second; <1 GB GPU memory.
- Model vectors pick up traits (e.g. "is a coding model") without being told.
- Main use in later work: adding new, unseen models with few labels (e.g. UniRoute).

## For Yugos
- Overlap: MMLU (Yugos uses MMLU-Pro), GPQA (Yugos uses GPQA Diamond; EmbedLLM has diamond variants), GSM8K. MedMCQA is close to MedQA but not the same. No code, no tau2.
- Model freshness: none. All 112 are small/old open models. Labels do not transfer to GPT-6.x, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 or DeepSeek V4.
- Effort data: none. One run per model, no cost or tokens.
- How to use:
  - Learn the method: "one vector per model" lets you add a new model with ~a few hundred labelled questions.
  - Our own version: build a small right/wrong matrix for Yugos's model+effort list. Treat each (model, effort) pair as one "model" row. Then fit MF.
  - Do not use its labels to train a Yugos router.

# Router benchmark step 13: RouteLLM data (2026-11-26)

- Who: LMSYS / UC Berkeley + Anyscale + Canva (Isaac Ong, Amjad Almahairi, Vincent Wu, Wei-Lin Chiang, Tianhao Wu, Joseph E. Gonzalez, M Waleed Kadous, Ion Stoica), June 2024 (v4 Feb 2025). Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18665 (ICLR 2025 (unverified)). Code: https://github.com/lm-sys/RouteLLM (Apache-2.0).
- Data: https://huggingface.co/routellm (7 datasets). Licence: Apache-2.0 on `gpt4_dataset` and `gpt4_judge_battles` (HF cards). The other 5 show no licence on HF; the Arena source set (`lmarena-ai/arena-human-preference-55k`) is Apache-2.0.
- Size: 109,101 GPT-4-judged prompts + 10,000 validation, ~55–65k human Arena battles, 1,531 MMLU battles.
- Only 2 models answer in the routellm data (GPT-4 vs Mixtral). Labels are "which of the two is better", not right/wrong per model.

### Files (checked on HF 2026-11-26)
- `gpt4_dataset`: `train.jsonl` 290 MB (109,101 rows), `valid.jsonl` 26.7 MB (10,000 rows).
  - Columns: `prompt`, `source` (list), `gpt4_response`, `mixtral_response`, `mixtral_score` (1–5, given by GPT-4).
  - Score spread (train): 5 = 74,728; 4 = 19,621; 3 = 4,616; 2 = 5,018; 1 = 5,118. So Mixtral is "good enough" (4–5) on 86% of prompts.
- `gpt4_judge_battles`: 1 parquet 167 MB, 109,101 rows. The same prompts as pairwise battles.
  - Columns: `id`, `model_a` (gpt-4-1106-preview), `model_b` (mixtral-8x7b-instruct-v0.1), `prompt`, `response_a`, `response_b`, `winner_model_a`, `winner_model_b`, `winner_tie`.
- `mmlu_battles`: 1 parquet 0.9 MB, 1,531 rows. Same columns. Built from MMLU validation answers (ids 14042–15572).
  - GPT-4 wins 17.6%, Mixtral wins 5.3%, tie 77.1% (both right or both wrong).
- `lmsys-arena-human-preference-55k-thresholds`: 57,477 rows. Columns `id`, `bert`, `causal_llm`, `sw_ranking`, `mf` = each router's score per Arena prompt. Used to calibrate routing thresholds.
- `arena_battles_embeddings` (55,361 rows), `gpt4_judge_battles_embeddings` (109,101 rows, 735 MB), `mmlu_battles_embeddings` (1,531 rows): only an `embeddings` vector column (OpenAI embeddings (unverified)).
- Raw Arena battles: not in the routellm org. Use `lmarena-ai/arena-human-preference-55k` (57,477 rows, 64 models; A wins 34.9%, B wins 34.2%, tie 30.9%).

## Sub-benchmarks (training data + 3 eval sets)
| Area | Benchmark | Prompts (HF data) |
|---|---|---|
| Chat (train, GPT-4 judge) | lmsys-chat-1m | 34,329 |
| Chat (train, GPT-4 judge) | ShareGPT | 22,060 |
| Chat (train, GPT-4 judge) | Anthropic HH | 17,332 |
| Instruction (train, GPT-4 judge) | FLAN v2 NIv2 | 10,400 |
| Instruction (train, GPT-4 judge) | Evol-Instruct | 9,112 |
| Chat (train, GPT-4 judge) | UltraChat | 8,713 |
| Reasoning (train, GPT-4 judge) | FLAN v2 CoT | 2,587 |
| QA (train, GPT-4 judge) | FalseQA | 2,114 |
| Instruction (train, GPT-4 judge) | FLAN v2 P3 | 1,512 |
| QA (train, GPT-4 judge) | TruthfulQA | 737 |
| Instruction (train, GPT-4 judge) | FLAN v2 FLAN2021 | 371 |
| **gpt4_dataset train total** | (161 rows have 2–3 sources) | **109,101** |
| gpt4_dataset validation | same 11 sources | 10,000 |
| Chat (train, human votes) | Chatbot Arena battles | 57,477 public file (paper: 65k after cleaning, from 80k) |
| Knowledge (train, gold labels) | MMLU validation | 1,531 |
| Eval | MT-Bench | 160 (80 questions × 2 turns) — paper only |
| Eval | MMLU test | 14,042 — paper only |
| Eval | GSM8K | "over 1,000" (GSM8K test = 1,319) — paper only |

- Source counts: my own count of `train.jsonl` and `valid.jsonl` (2026-11-26). Prompts come from the Nectar dataset (from earlier notes).
- Math and code prompts are mixed into the chat sources. They have no tag, so they can't be counted alone.

## Models
- Answer models in routellm files (2): gpt-4-1106-preview (strong), mixtral-8x7b-instruct-v0.1 (weak).
- Judge: GPT-4 (scores Mixtral 1–5; ~120k samples, ~$700).
- Arena battles: 64 models, grouped into 10 tiers. Strong = tiers 0–1, weak = tier 2.
  - OpenAI: gpt-4-0125-preview, gpt-4-1106-preview, gpt-4-0613, gpt-4-0314, gpt-3.5-turbo (0125/0613/1106/0314)
  - Anthropic: claude-1, claude-2.0, claude-2.1, claude-instant-1
  - Google: gemini-pro, gemini-pro-dev-api, palm-2
  - Mistral: mistral-medium, mixtral-8x7b-instruct-v0.1, mistral-7b-instruct (v0.1/v0.2), nous-hermes-2-mixtral-8x7b-dpo
  - Others: qwen1.5-72b/7b/4b-chat, qwen-14b-chat, yi-34b-chat, deepseek-llm-67b-chat, llama-2-70b/13b/7b-chat, vicuna-33b/13b/7b, wizardlm-70b/13b, tulu-2-dpo-70b, openchat-3.5 (+0106), starling-lm-7b-alpha, solar-10.7b, zephyr-7b alpha/beta, pplx-70b/7b-online, codellama-34b-instruct, falcon-180b-chat, chatglm 6b/2/3, koala-13b, alpaca-13b, dolly-v2-12b, mpt-7b/30b-chat, RWKV-4-Raven-14B, llama-13b, and others
- Generalization tests in paper (no retraining): Claude 3 Opus / Claude 3 Sonnet, Llama 3.1 70B / Llama 3.1 8B.

## Key findings
- Routers: `mf` (matrix factorization, recommended), `sw_ranking` (similarity-weighted Elo), `bert`, `causal_llm` (Llama-3-8B classifier), `random`.
- MT-Bench: best MF router reaches 50% of the GPT-4-vs-Mixtral gap with only 13.4% GPT-4 calls (random needs 49%). That is ~3.7× cheaper at 95% of GPT-4 quality.
- MMLU and GSM8K savings are small: ~1.4–1.5× at the 50% point. Arena data alone helped little here. The 1.5k MMLU gold labels helped most on MMLU.
- Data augmentation matters more than router type. GPT-4-judge data gave the biggest jump on MT-Bench.
- Routers transfer to new model pairs without retraining (APGR ~0.77 on Claude 3 Opus/Sonnet).

## For Yugos
- Overlap: MMLU (Yugos has MMLU-Pro), GSM8K, MT-Bench-style chat (close to Arena-Hard v2). TruthfulQA prompts only. No code labels, no agentic.
- Model freshness: none. All models are 2023–early 2024.
- Effort data: none.
- Binary only: strong vs weak. Yugos picks among many providers, models and efforts. So this does not fit directly.
- How to use:
  - Real chat prompts (lmsys-chat-1m, ShareGPT) are a good pool of "chat/QA" questions to re-label with new models.
  - The `mixtral_score` idea works for Yugos: a strong judge scores the cheap answer 1–5; escalate only when the score is low.
  - The threshold calibration method (set a % of strong calls) fits a cost budget.
  - Do not use the GPT-4/Mixtral labels as truth for today's models.

# Router benchmark step 14: MixInstruct / LLM-Blender (2026-11-26)

- Who: Allen Institute for AI + USC + Zhejiang University (Dongfu Jiang, Xiang Ren, Bill Yuchen Lin), June 2023. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.02561 (ACL 2023 main). Code: https://github.com/yuchenlin/LLM-Blender
- Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/llm-blender/mix-instruct (1.54 GB). Licence: MIT (HF card).
  - Files: `train_data_prepared.jsonl` 1.38 GB, `val_data_prepared.jsonl` 68.7 MB, `test_data_prepared.jsonl` 86.3 MB.
- Columns (one row = one instruction with all model answers):
  - `id` (e.g. `unified_chip2/69962`), `instruction`, `input`, `output` (reference answer, from GPT-4/ChatGPT/human).
  - `candidates`: list of 12 answers. Each has `model`, `decoding_method`, `text`, `scores` (logprobs, BLEU, ROUGE-1/2/L/Lsum, BERTScore; README tables also show BLEURT and BARTScore).
  - `cmp_results`: JSON string of ChatGPT pairwise votes ("A is better", "B is better", "Same good", "Same bad"). Only in test (4,771 rows); `null` elsewhere.
- Size: 110,000 instructions (train 100,000 / val 5,000 / test 5,000) × 11 models in the paper (12 names in the files) ≈ 1.3M answers.
- No right/wrong labels. Quality = text-overlap metrics vs a reference, plus ChatGPT pairwise ranks on test.

## Sub-benchmarks (4 sources)
| Area | Benchmark | Prompts (paper Table 1) |
|---|---|---|
| Instruction (GPT-4 answers) | Alpaca-GPT4 (`itwgpt4`) | 22,862 |
| Instruction (human answers) | Dolly-15K (`dolly_15k`) | 7,584 |
| Chat / instruction (ChatGPT answers) | GPT4All-LAION (`unified_chip2`, `laion`) | 76,552 |
| Chat (ChatGPT answers) | ShareGPT (`sharegpt`) | 3,002 |
| **Total** | | **110,000** |

- My count of the HF files (2026-11-26):
  - Test 5,000: unified_chip2 3,478 · itwgpt4 1,027 · dolly_15k 347 · sharegpt 145 · laion 3. ChatGPT votes on 4,771 (229 blocked by the API filter).
  - Val 5,000: unified_chip2 3,394 · itwgpt4 1,081 · dolly_15k 379 · sharegpt 138 · laion 8.
  - Train 100,000: not counted (1.38 GB file).
- Mostly short, everyday instructions (avg ~20 tokens in, ~66 out). No math, code or agent sets.

## Models (11 in paper; 12 names in data, all open, early 2023)
- Top tier by ChatGPT rank: Open Assistant (oasst-sft-4-pythia-12b-epoch-3.5), Vicuna (vicuna-13b-1.1), Alpaca (alpaca-native, 7B)
- Middle: Baize (llama-7b-hf-baize-lora-bf16), MOSS (moss-moon-003-sft), ChatGLM (chatglm-6b), Koala (koala-7B-HF)
- Bottom: Dolly v2 (dolly-v2-12b), Mosaic MPT (mpt-7b-instruct; data also has base mpt-7b), StableLM (stablelm-tuned-alpha-7b), Flan-T5 (flan-t5-xxl)
- Judge: ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo, early 2023).

## Key findings
- No single model wins. Open Assistant is best on average (GPT-Rank 3.90 of 11), but Koala (rank 6.76) is as good or better than both top models on ~40% of prompts.
- PairRanker (compares two answers at a time) picks best: GPT-Rank 3.20, top-3 hit 65.1%. Random pick = 6.14.
- LLM-Blender (PairRanker top-3 + GenFuser that merges them) beats every single model: GPT-Rank 3.01; as good or better than Open Assistant on 77.7%.
- Picking by BARTScore is a good cheap stand-in for ChatGPT judging.

## For Yugos
- Overlap: none with Yugos benchmarks. Only general chat instructions.
- Model freshness: none. All 2023 7B–13B models.
- Effort data: none. No cost, no tokens, no latency.
- Labels are fuzzy (BLEU/ROUGE vs reference, ChatGPT pairwise). Yugos scores right/wrong and cost.
- How to use:
  - Idea only: pairwise ranking ("is answer A better than B?") and fusing top answers. Fusion is not a routing choice in Yugos, so low value.
  - Prompt pool: Dolly and ShareGPT prompts could add chat variety if re-run on new models.
  - Not useful as training labels.

# Router benchmark step 15: SCOPE-60K / SCOPE-250 / SCOPE-OOD (2026-11-26)

- Who: UC San Diego, PXie Lab (Qi Cao, Shuhao Zhang, Ruiyi Zhang, Peijia Qin, Pengtao Xie) + Ruizhe Zhou (independent), Jan 2026. Paper: "Models Under SCOPE", https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22323 (CC BY 4.0). ICML 2026 (unverified; slides found on icml.cc). Project: https://sullivan07043.github.io/SCOPE · Code: https://github.com/Sullivan07043/SCOPE · Router model: https://huggingface.co/Cooolder/SCOPE
- Data (now released, fixes my earlier "not released" note):
  - https://huggingface.co/datasets/Cooolder/SCOPE-60K — Apache-2.0. Parquet: `train` 92.3 MB, `test` 3.4 MB, `anchor` 2.4 MB.
  - https://huggingface.co/datasets/Cooolder/SCOPE-OOD-set — Apache-2.0. Parquet: `test` 5.8 MB, `anchor` 4.1 MB.
- Columns (one row = question × model): `id`, `prompt`, `model` (OpenRouter id), `model_name`, `raw_output`, `response`, `final_answer`, `gt`, `is_correct`, `category`, `domain`, `reasoning_mode` (bool), `usage_cost` (USD), `usage_prompt_tokens`, `usage_completion_tokens`, `usage_total_tokens`, `score_info`, `error`. The OOD set adds `reasoning`, `inference_backend` (all "openrouter"), `multimodal_mode`.
- Size (my count, 2026-11-26):
  - SCOPE-60K: train 62,114 rows = 4,778 questions × 13 models; test 3,276 = 252 × 13; anchor 3,250 = 250 × 13. "60K" = rows, not questions.
  - Unique questions: 5,030 (train + test) + 250 anchor (96 anchor prompts also appear in train).
  - SCOPE-OOD: test 1,250 = 250 new questions × 5 models; anchor 1,250 = the same 250 anchor questions × 5 models.

## Sub-benchmarks (5 in-distribution sources + anchor + 5 OOD sources)
| Area | Benchmark | Prompts (HF data) |
|---|---|---|
| Chinese exam (multi-subject) | GAOKAO (2010–2022 MCQ: politics 307, history 265, math II 210, math I 203, biology 144, chemistry 119, English 265, physics 63, Chinese 81, geography 33) | 1,690 train + 91 test |
| Knowledge | MMLU-Pro | 1,436 train + 63 test |
| Reasoning (STEM) | R-Bench (English) | 1,038 train + 56 test |
| Science | GPQA (variant not stated) | 414 train + 34 test |
| Other | "Forum" questions (source not described) | 200 train + 8 test |
| **SCOPE-60K total** | | **4,778 train + 252 test = 5,030** |
| Anchor quiz | SCOPE-250 (ids hidden as `anchor000`–; chemistry 45, math 41, physics 30, biology 29, others ≤12) | 250 |
| OOD | Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) | 104 |
| OOD | OlympiadBench | 68 |
| OOD | SimpleQA | 50 |
| OOD | AIME 2024 | 15 |
| OOD | AIME 2025 | 13 |
| **SCOPE-OOD total** | | **250** |

- Source names come from `id` prefixes (`2010-2022_*`, `mmlu_pro_*`, `rbench_en_*`, `gpqa_*`, `Forum-*`, `hle_*`, `olympiad*`, `simpleqa_*`, `aime_2024_*`, `aime2025-*`).
- Paper domain mix (Fig. 3): math 29.7%, chemistry 20.2%, physics 18.0%, history 21.4%, politics 20.7%, Chinese 18.0%.
- No code and no agentic tasks.

## Models
- Seen pool, SCOPE-60K (13, via OpenRouter; some rows on `:free` endpoints):
  - Reasoning on (`reasoning_mode` = True, 6): deepseek-r1t2-chimera (TNG), qwen3-235b-a22b, qwen3-14b, gpt-oss-20b, nemotron-nano-9b-v2, nova-2-lite-v1
  - Reasoning off (7): llama-3.1-8b-instruct, llama-3.3-70b-instruct, gemma-3-4b-it, gemma-3-12b-it, gemma-3-27b-it, ministral-3b, ministral-8b
  - Train accuracy: deepseek-r1t2-chimera 75.8%, nova-2-lite 65.1%, qwen3-14b 63.0%, gpt-oss-20b 61.5%, qwen3-235b 58.3%, gemma-3-27b 53.1%, nemotron-nano 53.0%, llama-3.3-70b 52.2%, gemma-3-12b 47.4%, ministral-8b 37.3%, gemma-3-4b 35.5%, ministral-3b 32.8%, llama-3.1-8b 29.6%.
  - Paper says it trained on 7 of these (DeepSeek-R1T2-Chimera, Qwen3-235B, Nova-2-Lite, Qwen3-14B, GPT-OSS-20B, Llama-3.3-70B, Gemma-3-27B).
- Unseen pool, SCOPE-OOD (5, all reasoning on): claude-sonnet-4.5, gpt-5-mini, gemini-3-flash-preview, deepseek-v3.2, grok-4.1-fast.
  - The paper names only 4 unseen models. Gemini-3-flash is in the data but not in the paper text I read.
  - OOD test accuracy: gemini-3-flash 65.6%, grok-4.1-fast 44.4%, gpt-5-mini 42.0%, claude-sonnet-4.5 40.4%, deepseek-v3.2 39.6%.
  - Anchor accuracy: 77–80% for all 5 (the anchor quiz is easy for these models).
- Router backbone: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, trained with RL.

## Key findings
- SCOPE does not pick a model directly. It predicts each model's accuracy and token cost, then picks with a user knob α (accuracy vs cost).
- To handle a new model, it only needs that model's answers on the 250 anchor questions. It finds similar anchor questions and reasons from them.
- In-distribution test (α = 1): 75.0% accuracy at $0.63 vs best baseline Graph Router 73.0% at $0.72.
- OOD (unseen models): 50.8% accuracy at $3.08. Paper claims +25.7% accuracy vs Claude-Sonnet-4.5 alone at 74% lower cost; up to 95.1% cost cut in cheap mode.
- Its own reasoning is short: ~239 tokens per decision.

## For Yugos
- Overlap: MMLU-Pro, GPQA (not stated if Diamond), HLE, SimpleQA, AIME 2024, AIME 2025. That is 6 Yugos benchmarks, but small counts (13–1,436).
- Model freshness: partial. OOD models are late-2025 (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5-mini, Gemini 3 Flash, DeepSeek V3.2). No GPT-6.x, Claude 5.x, Gemini 4 or DeepSeek V4.
- Effort data: only on/off (`reasoning_mode`), one setting per model. No low/medium/high levels. But every row has real cost and token counts.
- How to use:
  - Best idea for Yugos: the anchor quiz. Run Yugos's model+effort list on 250 fixed questions, then route new questions by "how did each option do on similar anchor questions". New models only need 250 runs.
  - Swap the anchor set for Yugos-style questions (add code and tau2).
  - The OOD rows (HLE, SimpleQA, AIME) with cost and tokens are a small but real test set for "accuracy per dollar" on 2025 models.
