# Router benchmark step 16: RouteabilityBench / RAP (2026-11-26)

- Who: Yihang Lu (Sorbonne Université / iEES), Denica Kjorvezir, Ana Gjorgjevikj, Tome Eftimov (Jožef Stefan Institute, Ljubljana), Carola Doerr (LIP6, Sorbonne). NeurIPS 2026 poster. Paper: "Routeability Before Routing", https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34825 (posted 2026-11-25, CC BY 4.0). Poster: https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/poster/139509
- Data: https://github.com/sebastianlu0414/RouteabilityBench — 1 commit, one folder `RouteabilityBench_CC-BY-4.0_RELEASE_CANDIDATE`. Licence: CC BY 4.0 by folder name; the paper says licence checks are still a pre-release step (unverified).
  - What it ships (paper): frozen split manifests, a prompt-ID registry, derived score and evidence tables, metadata for each model, claim-check scripts, a HELM rebuild manifest (264 files with SHA-256). One named file: `e1_inference_robustness.csv`.
  - What it does not ship: embeddings, prediction caches, router training code. So you cannot retrain routers from it alone.
  - File columns: not described in the paper; repo contents not readable via fetch (unverified).
- Score source: HELM Capabilities release v1.15.0 (dated 2025-11-24) per-instance outputs. Raw answers are public at `storage.googleapis.com/crfm-helm-public/capabilities/benchmark_output/releases/v1.15.0/`.
  - Metrics: `chain_of_thought_correctness` (GPQA, MMLU-Pro; 0/1), `ifeval_strict_accuracy` (IFEval; 5 levels), `omni_math_accuracy` (Omni-MATH; 5 levels).
- Size: 2,987 prompts × 66 models ≈ 197k scores.
- Cost: only a parameter-size proxy, not real API prices. No latency.

## Sub-benchmarks (4; WildBench dropped)
| Area | Benchmark | Prompts (paper) |
|---|---|---|
| Science | GPQA (HELM subset; 445 in some analyses) | 446 |
| Knowledge | MMLU-Pro (HELM sample) | 1,000 |
| Instruction following | IFEval | 541 |
| Math (olympiad) | Omni-MATH (HELM sample; 998 in some analyses) | 1,000 |
| **Total** | | **2,987** |

- Which GPQA subset (main/diamond) HELM uses: not stated in the paper (unverified).
- HELM Capabilities also has WildBench. The paper excluded it.

## Models (66 of 68 eligible in HELM Capabilities v1.15.0)
- The paper gives no names, only counts: 22 open weights, 8 gated, 36 closed.
- The 68 eligible models (my check of HELM `runs_to_run_suites.json`, all have all 4 scenarios). Which 2 were dropped is not stated (unverified).
  - OpenAI (13): gpt-5.1, gpt-5, gpt-5-mini, gpt-5-nano, o3, o4-mini, gpt-4.1, gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-oss-120b, gpt-oss-20b
  - Anthropic (9): claude-sonnet-4.5, claude-haiku-4.5, claude-opus-4, claude-opus-4-thinking-10k, claude-sonnet-4, claude-sonnet-4-thinking-10k, claude-3.7-sonnet, claude-3.5-sonnet, claude-3.5-haiku
  - Google (8): gemini-3-pro-preview, gemini-2.5-pro-preview, gemini-2.5-flash-preview, gemini-2.5-flash-lite, gemini-2.0-flash, gemini-2.0-flash-lite, gemini-1.5-pro, gemini-1.5-flash
  - xAI (3): grok-4, grok-3-beta, grok-3-mini-beta
  - DeepSeek (2): deepseek-r1-0528, deepseek-v3
  - Qwen (5): qwen3-235b-a22b, qwen3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507, qwen3-next-80b-a3b-thinking, qwen2.5-72b, qwen2.5-7b
  - Meta (5): llama-4-maverick, llama-4-scout, llama-3.1-405b/70b/8b
  - Mistral (5): mistral-large-2411, mistral-small-2503, mistral-7b-v0.3, mixtral-8x22b, mixtral-8x7b
  - Amazon (4): nova-premier, nova-pro, nova-lite, nova-micro
  - Writer (4): palmyra-x5, palmyra-x-004, palmyra-fin, palmyra-med
  - IBM (3): granite-4.0-h-small, granite-4.0-micro, granite-3.3-8b
  - AllenAI (4): olmo-2-32b, olmo-2-13b, olmo-2-7b, olmoe-1b-7b
  - Others (3): kimi-k2-instruct, glm-4.5-air, marin-8b-instruct

## Key findings
- Main point: check if a benchmark is "routeable" before claiming routing gains.
- Headroom (best-per-prompt oracle minus single best model):
  - Omni-MATH: 0.722 → 0.922 (+0.200). Unique best model on 8.4% of prompts.
  - GPQA: 0.803 → 0.996 (+0.193). Unique best on 1.1%.
  - MMLU-Pro: 0.903 → 0.994 (+0.091). Unique best on 0.8%.
  - IFEval: 0.951 → 0.996 (+0.045). Unique best on 0.0%.
- Ties kill routing: on a typical prompt, 36% (Omni-MATH) to 88% (IFEval) of the 66 models share the top score.
- Common router upgrades (more embeddings, PCA, abstain option, clustering, stronger regressors) do not beat "always use the single best model" in a reliable way.
  - Gap closure of forced routing is negative on GPQA (−0.135), MMLU-Pro (−0.147), IFEval (−0.324). So routing is worse than the single best model there.
  - Only Omni-MATH shows a small gain (+0.081 gap closure; Δ regret −0.0136). It is not significant after family-wise correction (Holm p = 0.091).
- They ask papers to report: headroom, tied-best stats, how the model pool was built, and corrected statistical tests.

## For Yugos
- Overlap: MMLU-Pro and GPQA (Yugos uses GPQA Diamond). Omni-MATH is close to Yugos math (AIME, MATH). IFEval is not on the Yugos list.
- Model freshness: partial. Newest are GPT-5.1, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro preview, Grok 4 (late 2025). No GPT-6.x, Claude 5.x, Gemini 4, DeepSeek V4.
- Effort data: very little. Only Claude Opus 4 / Sonnet 4 with "thinking-10k" vs no thinking, and some thinking vs instruct model pairs (Qwen3).
- How to use:
  - Most useful as a warning. On saturated sets (MMLU-Pro, IFEval) almost every strong model is right, so the gain comes from picking the cheapest right model, not the smartest.
  - For Yugos, measure headroom and tie rates per benchmark first. Spend router effort on sets with real headroom (math, GPQA-hard, HLE, agentic).
  - Since quality ties are common, cost and latency decide the winner. RAP has no real cost data, so add your own.
  - Raw HELM answers for these 68 models can be pulled from the HELM bucket if you want per-question labels.

# Router benchmark step 17: SWE-Router trajectories (2026-11-26)

- Who: University College London (Seongho Son, Shuhan Wang, Lorenz Wolf, Ilija Bogunovic) + UNIST (Sangwoong Yoon) + PSL (Jiahua Tang) + Univ. of Basel (Bogunovic), June 2026. Paper: "SWE-Router: Routing in Multi-turn Agentic Software Engineering Tasks", https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00053 (CC BY 4.0). ICML 2026 workshop (5th Deep Learning for Code).
- Data: HF org https://huggingface.co/SWE-Router (35 datasets, 2 LoRA router models, all public, updated Jan–May 2026).
  - The paper gives no data link. I matched the org to the paper because its numbers match paper Table 1 exactly (gpt-5-mini 55.6%, deepseek-v3.2 62.4%, gemini-3-pro 70.4% on SWE-bench Verified; split sizes 1,755 / 210 / 346). Link is very likely but (unverified).
  - Licence: none on any card (READMEs are auto-generated, no text). Treat as "no licence given".
- Columns (trajectory sets): `instance_id`, `problem_statement`, `messages` (full agent chat, mini-SWE-agent), `model`, `resolved` (bool, from unit tests), `instance_cost` (USD), `api_calls` (steps), `step_cost_list` (cost per step; most sets), `source_split` (v4 sets).
- Task sets: `swe-smith-traj-repowise-*` have `instance_id`, `patch`, `FAIL_TO_PASS`, `PASS_TO_PASS`, `image_name`, `repo`, `problem_statement`. `*rephrase_problem_statement*` have 1–3 reworded issue texts per task.
- Size:
  - Paper Table 1: 6,428 trajectories over 3 named models (gpt-5-mini 2,734, deepseek-v3.2 2,811, gemini-3-pro 883). Paper says 4 models but names 3.
  - HF org: ~44.5k trajectory rows over 9 models (my rough sum of split sizes, includes repeat runs `train_1`/`train_2`/`test_1`).
- Setup: mini-SWE-agent, 75-step budget (some HF sets go to 250 calls). Router looks at the cheap model's first K = 1–4 turns.

## Sub-benchmarks (3)
| Area | Benchmark | Prompts (HF data) |
|---|---|---|
| Agentic code (train/val/test, repo-disjoint) | SWE-smith subset "repowise v4" | 3,582 train + 210 val + 346 test = 4,138 tasks |
| Agentic code (older split) | SWE-smith subset "repowise v3" | 1,965 train + 346 val = 2,311 tasks |
| Agentic code (eval) | SWE-bench Verified | 500 |
| Agentic code (eval, multi-language) | SWE-bench Multilingual | 300 |

- Paper uses SWE-smith 1,755 / 210 / 346 (train/val/test) + SWE-bench Verified 500. The v4 4k set and Multilingual look like later extensions (unverified).

## Models (9 on HF; 3–4 in paper)
- Paper: gpt-5-mini (weak), deepseek-v3.2 (weak), gemini-3-pro-preview (strong), 4th not named. HF suggests the 4th is claude-opus-4.7 (unverified).
- SWE-bench Verified on HF (500 each; resolve rate, mean cost per task, mean steps):
  - claude-opus-4.7: 78.2%, $0.32, 18 steps
  - gpt-5.2 (`gpt-5.2-medium` = medium effort): 74.2%, $0.26, 16 steps
  - gemini-3-pro-preview: 70.4%, $0.78, 42 steps
  - gemini-3.1-pro-preview: 65.4%, $1.32, 39 steps
  - deepseek-v4-flash: 63.2%, $0.014, 51 steps
  - deepseek-v3.2: 62.4%, $0.045, 46 steps
  - gpt-5-mini: 55.6%, $0.033, 15 steps
  - gemini-2.5-pro: 50.0%, $0.35, 21 steps
  - gpt-5-nano: 30.6%, $0.036, 29 steps
- SWE-bench Multilingual (300 each): claude-opus-4.7 73.7%, deepseek-v4-flash 72.0%, gpt-5-mini 40.7%, gpt-5-nano 1.3%.
- SWE-smith test (v4, 346): claude-opus-4.7 268 resolved, gemini-3-pro 185, gpt-5-mini 165 (of 339), deepseek-v3.2 146.
- Router models: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B LoRA value heads (`SWE-Router/qwencoder7-lora32-...`).

## Key findings
- Task text alone can't tell a typo fix from a big refactor. Letting the cheap model explore for a few turns, then deciding, works better.
- Theory: reading the partial run never hurts routing, and helps when early turns are informative.
- SWE-bench Verified, Route-AUC: +12 points or more over the best text-only router; deepseek-v3.2 → strong reaches 0.780 at K = 2 (+15.3 pts over K = 0).
- Cost gap is huge: Gemini 3 Pro cost $391 for 500 Verified tasks vs $17 (gpt-5-mini) and $23 (deepseek-v3.2) — for +8 to +15 points.
- DeepSeek V4 Flash nearly matches V3.2 accuracy at about 1/3 of the cost.

## For Yugos
- Overlap: SWE-bench Verified (on Yugos list). Nothing for chat, math, tau2, Terminal-Bench or BFCL.
- Model freshness: good for 2026 mid-tier. Has claude-opus-4.7, gpt-5.2, gemini-3.1-pro, deepseek-v4-flash. No GPT-6.x, Claude Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.x, Gemini 4.
- Effort data: almost none. Only `gpt-5.2-medium` is labelled with an effort. One setting per model.
- Good for cost: every row has real USD cost, step count and per-step cost.
- How to use:
  - Best fit for Yugos agentic tasks: "start cheap, check after a few turns, then escalate". Yugos may only allow one pick per task; check if mid-task switching is allowed.
  - Per-task right/wrong + cost for 9 models on the same 500 Verified tasks = a ready routing table for that one benchmark.
  - Messages are full trajectories. Small parquet files are safe to read; large sets are hundreds of MB.
  - No licence: fine for study, ask before redistributing.

# Router benchmark step 20: AutoBench Router Benchmark, ARB (2026-11-26)

- Who: AutoBench (Peter Kruger). Blog 26 Oct 2026: https://huggingface.co/blog/PeterKruger/router-benchmark-2026-10. Site/board: https://autobench.org (also botscanner.ai/router).
- Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/AutoBench/router-benchmark-2026-10 (21.7 MB, CSV + parquet). Licence: CC-BY-4.0 (questions, scores, costs). Model answers included for audit.
- Files: `questions.csv` (252), `matrix.csv` (5,428 question×model rows: score, judge SD, billed USD), `answers.csv` (~5,040), `decisions.csv` (router picks), `pool.json` (20 models), `frozen_params.json`, `scoreboard.json` (28 passes), `wave3/` (Nov 2026 re-audit), `SHA256SUMS`.
- Size: 252 open-ended prompts × 20 models. Rules frozen 29 Aug 2026 (pre-registered) before any router call. Routers called 30 Aug – 1 Sep 2026.
- Type: offline "lookup" audit. Each router picks a model per prompt; its pick is graded from the stored answer matrix.

## Sub-benchmarks (prompt mix, from `questions.csv`)
| Split | Group | Prompts |
|---|---|---|
| Domain | History | 34 |
| Domain | Agentic tool use | 32 |
| Domain | Language | 31 |
| Domain | Science | 31 |
| Domain | Social science | 27 |
| Domain | Arts & recreation | 26 |
| Domain | Computer science / general | 22 |
| Domain | Technology | 19 |
| Domain | Literature | 16 |
| Domain | Philosophy & psychology | 14 |
| Skill | world_knowledge / math_reasoning / planning_agentic / creative_synthesis / coding | 107 / 61 / 35 / 27 / 22 |
| Difficulty | very simple / simple / medium / difficult / very difficult | 50 / 56 / 50 / 49 / 47 |
| Register | human casual / human professional / agent structured | 87 / 84 / 81 |
| **Total** | | **252** |

Counts from my own read of `questions.csv` (2026-11-26). Prompts are AutoBench-generated, not public benchmark items.

## Scoring
- Each answer scored (scale 1–5, unverified; mean scores ~4–4.8) by a committee of LLM judges ("Collective-LLM-as-a-Judge"). Blog says 10 judges; `pool.json` lists 14 judge models (the cheaper/mid 14 of the 20 pool models).
- Delta-Hit = share of prompts where the picked model's score is within a locked window (δ) of the top-3 models on that prompt. δ official = 0.30, signal δ = 0.20.
- Collapse = a pass that sends ≥90% of prompts to one model.
- Autobench Router Index (ARI): quality = Delta-Hit lift over random; cost = log score between fixed $ anchors; cost weight β = 0.2. Exact formula not in blog.
- 10,000 bootstrap resamples for significance.

## Routers tested (7 systems, 17 headline settings; 28 passes in scoreboard)
- Not Diamond (cost-quality knob 0–10; only 7 of 20 pool models in its catalog; + native catalog run)
- OpenRouter Auto (low / medium / high / max tiers, limited to the 20)
- OrcaRouter (cheapest / balanced / quality, constrained + native)
- Azure Model Router (cost / balanced / quality; only 3 of 20 models overlap)
- NadirClaw (self-hosted DistilBERT classifier)
- Brick (self-hosted skill matrix)
- In-house FrugalGPT-style cascade
- Wave 3 (Nov 2026): new OpenRouter Auto, Conifer, dari. AutoBench's own router modes (Quality / Balanced / Cost) also listed. Wave 3 numbers not read here (unverified).

## Single-model baselines (pool of 20)
- Top: GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Sonnet 5, Qwen3.8 Max, Grok 4.6, GLM-5.3, Muse Spark 1.2
- Mid: GPT-5.6 Luna, Kimi K2.6, Gemini 3.7 Flash, GLM-5.2, MiniMax M3, Grok 4.3, Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B
- Cheap: Qwen3.5-9B, DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, gpt-oss-120b, Gemma 4 31B, Hy3, Muse Glimmer 30B
- No GPT-6.x, Claude Opus 5.5 / Fable, Gemini 4 or DeepSeek V4 Pro.

## Results (Delta-Hit, $ per question)
- Always GPT-5.6 Sol: 87.5%, $0.079
- Always GPT-5.6 Luna: 85.3%, $0.0043
- Random pick: 64.7%, $0.0115
- Oracle (best per prompt): 100%, $0.034; cheapest-good-enough oracle: 100%, $0.0018
- Not Diamond knob 0: 87.5%, $0.079 (= always Sol). Knob 4: 80.3%, $0.060. Knob 5: 46.6% (below random).
- Azure quality: 85.3%, $0.065
- OpenRouter Auto high: 79.1%, $0.023; max: 78.3%, $0.029; low: 65.7%
- NadirClaw: 70.3%, $0.051
- Orca quality: 65.7%; cheapest/balanced: 39.3%
- Brick: 63.9%, $0.0031
- Cascade: 60.9%
- Key finding: no router setting beat "always Luna" on quality AND cost. Always-Luna ranks #1 on ARI.
- 5 of 17 settings collapsed to one model. Different vendors almost never agree (median same-pick = 0).

## For Yugos
- Closest public audit to Yugos's setting: modern models, real billed cost, mixed chat/math/code/agentic prompts.
- Main lesson: a single cheap-but-good model is a very hard baseline. Yugos routers must beat "always one mid model".
- Data is open (CC-BY) → 252 × 20 score+cost matrix can be used as small extra labels.
- Gaps: judge-scored open answers, not Yugos benchmarks; no Opus 5.5 / GPT-6; no effort levels; only 252 prompts.

# Router benchmark step 21: AIMultiple Router Benchmark (2026-11-26)

- Who: AIMultiple (industry analyst site). Page: https://aimultiple.com/llm-router (updated 18 Nov 2026, last note 24 Nov 2026).
- Data: free ZIP with chart/table summaries (7 CSV, 146 data points). Per-question data only for paid Premium. No licence stated.
- Size: 523 agentic text-to-SQL tasks. Router runs 13–16 Nov 2026; timing rounds 25 Nov 2026 (20 questions × 8 rounds).
- Type: live audit. Each router is called through its real API.

## Sub-benchmarks (1 task type)
| Area | Benchmark | Tasks |
|---|---|---|
| Agentic SQL | AIMultiple text-to-SQL (built on BIRD); agent must first pick 1 of 11 aliased databases, then write SQL | 523 |
| **Total** | | **523** |

- Limits: up to 10 model calls per question, 600 s per request.

## Scoring
- Correct only if the agent picks the right database AND the query returns the reference result. Errors = fail.
- 95% bootstrap CIs over 523 questions. Pairwise: exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted, 5% level.
- Cost = $ per 1,000 questions. Latency = median seconds per question.

## Routers tested (8)
- NVIDIA Switchyard (GPT-6.1 Sol + Luna): 56.2%, $16.6/1K, 15.5 s
- OpenRouter Auto Code: 52.8%, $24.6, 11.1 s

# Router benchmark step 23: Epoch AI Benchmarking Hub (2026-11-26)

- Who: Epoch AI (non-profit research group). Page: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks. Data page: https://epoch.ai/benchmarks/use-this-data
- Data: ZIP https://epoch.ai/data/benchmark_data.zip (updated 2026-11-26). 92 files: 89 CSVs, README, 1 JSON. There is also a Python client (`pip install epochai`, reads the Airtable API).
- Licence: CC BY 4.0 for Epoch's data. The questions and answers still belong to each benchmark's creators.
- Size: one CSV per benchmark. One row = one **model + effort level** with its score. 975 rows are for the newest models (GPT-6.x, Claude Opus 5 / 5.5, Fable 5.x, Gemini 4, DeepSeek V4).
- Per-question data: only for **in-house runs** (Epoch ran the model itself). These rows have a `Logs` column that links to an Inspect `.eval` file. Benchmarks marked "external" have scores only.

## Sub-benchmarks

In-house runs (these can have per-question logs). Newest = rows for the newest models. "Public logs" = rows with a link to the `production-public` S3 bucket.

| Benchmark | Questions | Rows (all models) | Newest-model rows | Newest with public logs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPQA Diamond | 198 | 344 | 28 | 22 |

| **Total newest rows with public logs** | | | | **89** |

External runs (scores only, copied from other leaderboards). Those that overlap with Yugos:
- HLE (56 rows, 16 newest), Terminal-Bench (204 / 39), LiveBench (64 / 4), ARC-AGI 1 and 2 (338 / 124, 316 / 119), MMLU (249 / 3).
- Old, easy sets with no newest models: GSM8K (235), HellaSwag (135), Winogrande (145), ARC AI2 (145), BBH (92), TriviaQA, PIQA, BoolQ.
- Others with many newest rows: SciCode (88), CritPt (85), DTBench (83), LMCA (80), SimpleBench (38), Aider Polyglot (8), WebDev Arena (30), WeirdML (30).

Question counts come from my earlier count file (`sn34_benchmark_question_counts_2026-11-23.md`) and from the score fractions (e.g. 0.9122807 = 260/285). The FrontierMath, chess and MirrorCode counts are my estimates.

## Models (newest; in-house GPQA Diamond rows)
- **OpenAI (GPT-6.x):**
  - gpt-6.2-astra_max (2026-11-17, **no log yet**)
  - gpt-6.1-terra_max, gpt-6.1-sol_max (logs)
  - gpt-6-astra_max, gpt-6-sol_max, gpt-6-luna_max (logs)
  - Chess also has `gpt-6-astra_promax`. MirrorCode has `gpt-6-astra_high`.
- **Anthropic:**
  - claude-opus-5-5_max (2026-09-22, logs). MirrorCode also has `_high` (no log).
  - claude-fable-5-2_max (2026-11-09, **no log yet**)
  - claude-fable-5-1_max (logs on OTIS, SimpleQA, chess, MirrorCode)
  - claude-fable-5 `_low` / `_high` / `_max` (logs); SimpleQA has `_xhigh`
  - claude-opus-5 / `_low` / `_max` (logs)
  - `-fallback_max` rows (e.g. claude-opus-5-5-fallback_max) have no logs. Their meaning is not explained (unverified: probably a rerun of refused or failed questions).
- **Google (Gemini 4):** gemini-4-neon_xhigh, gemini-4-hydrogen_xhigh (logs); gemini-4-argon_high (logs); gemini-4-carbon_high (**no log yet**).
- **DeepSeek V4:** v4-pro `_none` / `_high` / `_max`, v4-pro-0813_max, v4-flash-0731_max, v4.1-flash_max, v4.1-flash-1017_max (all with logs on GPQA).
- **Effort suffixes in the in-house files (row counts):** high 190, max 185, xhigh 108, low 86, none 80, medium 42, minimal 28, token budgets (16K / 27K / 32K / 59K / 64K) 49, promax 2. So effort levels are separate rows.
- Pattern: the newest model of each lab (GPT-6.2, Fable 5.2, Gemini 4 Carbon) has scores but no log yet. Logs seem to come a few weeks after the score.

## Log format
- Each `Logs` link is an Inspect AI `.eval` file, e.g. `https://epoch-benchmarks-production-public.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/inspect_ai_logs/6gmbahPSxHf9xVhAYqpnhi.eval` (Opus 5.5, GPQA).
- There is also a `Log viewer` link (`logs.epoch.ai/inspect-viewer/...`) that shows each question in the browser.
- **Access check today:** a direct request to the S3 link gave **403 Access Denied** from this machine. `logs.epoch.ai` gave 405. Bucket listing is denied. So bulk download may now be blocked or need the viewer (unverified; try again from a browser).
- Inside a `.eval` file (Inspect standard, not checked on these files): a ZIP with `header.json` (model, settings, total tokens) and one `samples/<id>_epoch_<n>.json` per question per try. Each holds the input, model output, score, token use and time.
- Most in-house runs use several tries per question (e.g. OTIS 0.9972 = 359/360 = 45 questions × 8 tries; unverified).

## For Yugos
- **Overlap with Yugos list:** GPQA Diamond, SimpleQA (Verified), AIME (OTIS mock AIME 2024–2025), MATH (Level 5), SWE-bench Verified. HLE, Terminal-Bench, LiveBench, ARC, Winogrande, HellaSwag, GSM8K are score-only here.
- **Best part:** the newest models at several effort levels on the same questions. This fits provider + model + effort routing.
- **How to join into a router table:**
  1. Pick a benchmark (e.g. GPQA Diamond).
  2. For each model + effort row with a log, open the `.eval` file and read each sample: question id, score, output tokens.
  3. Make one row per question id, with one column per model + effort (right/wrong, or mean over tries).
  4. Add cost = tokens × list price (logs have tokens, not dollars).
- **Size is small:** about 198 + 45 + 1,000 + 100 = ~1,350 questions with public newest-model logs. Good for labels, too small to train on alone.
- **Gaps:**
  - No per-question data for external benchmarks (HLE, Terminal-Bench, LiveBench, etc.).
  - FrontierMath logs are private.
  - SWE-bench Verified has only one newest row, in a staging bucket.
  - Newest models (GPT-6.2, Fable 5.2, Gemini 4 Carbon) have no logs yet.
  - Log download returned 403 from here today. Check access before planning on it.

# Router benchmark step 24: MathArena outputs (2026-11-26)

- Who: ETH Zurich SRI Lab (Balunović, Dekoninck, Vechev and others), 2025. Site: https://matharena.ai. Code: https://github.com/eth-sri/matharena (MIT licence).
- Data: HF org https://huggingface.co/MathArena — 114 datasets. 50 are `*_outputs` (model answers); the rest are the problem sets.
- Licence: code MIT. Output datasets: licence not checked per dataset (unverified).
- Size: one row = one **attempt** by one model on one problem. Usually 2–4 attempts per model per problem (e.g. AIME 2026: 120 rows per model = 30 problems × 4).
- Columns (same in all outputs sets): `problem_idx`, `problem`, `model_name`, `model_config`, `idx_answer`, `all_messages` (full trace), `answer`, `parsed_answer`, `gold_answer`, `correct`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cost`, `input_cost_per_tokens`, `output_cost_per_tokens`, `source`. **Cost and tokens are included.**

## Sub-benchmarks
Problems from my count file; newest-model rows from HF filter queries today.

| Set | Problems | Newest models present? |
|---|---|---|
| AIME 2025 / 2026, HMMT Feb 2025 / Feb 2026 / Nov 2025, BRUMO, SMT, CMIMC, Apex, Apex shortlist | 335 total | Only DeepSeek V4 (Pro / Flash). No GPT-6, Claude 5.x, Gemini 4 |

| SmallMath (new, updated 2026-11-24) | ~600 (unverified; 33,600 rows / 28 configs / 2 tries) | **Yes: GPT-6.x, Opus 5.5, Gemini 4, DeepSeek V4.1 at low/medium/high effort** |

| **Total** | **~2,100** | |

## Models (newest)

  - ArXivMath / BrokenArXiv: GPT-6 Astra (max), GPT-6 Astra (low), GPT-6 Sol (max), GPT-6.1 Sol (max).
  - SmallMath (subscription, 8 configs): gpt-6.2-sol low, gpt-6.2-astra low, gpt-6.1-sol low / high, gpt-6.1-terra low / medium, gpt-6-luna low / medium.
- **Claude Opus 5.5 — yes.**
  - opus_55_high in ArXivMath 05/26 – 10/26, BrokenArXiv, ArXivLean 09/26. opus_55_max in ArXivMath 06/26.
  - claude-opus-5.5-low (via OpenRouter) in SmallMath.
  - Also Claude Opus 5 (max), Sonnet 5.5 low and Haiku 5.5 low (SmallMath).

# Router benchmark step 25: LiveBench (2026-11-26)

- Who: Abacus.AI + NYU + others (Colin White, Yann LeCun, Micah Goldblum and others), 2024. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.19314. Code: https://github.com/LiveBench/LiveBench. Site: https://livebench.ai

- Licence: shown in the repo LICENSE file (type not checked; unverified, probably Apache 2.0).
- Size of per-question model data on HF:
  - `model_answer`: 93,715 rows (question_id, model_id, full answer text, category, task). **Last updated 2024-10-22.**
  - `model_judgment`: 60,372 rows (question_id, model, score 0–1, task, category). **Last updated 2025-04-07.** 195 models.
- Questions are scored by fixed rules (no LLM judge), so a judgment row = right/wrong per question.

## Sub-benchmarks
| Category | Questions (HF, release ≤ 2024-11) | Example tasks |
|---|---|---|
| Reasoning | 200 | web_of_lies, zebra_puzzle, spatial; later theory_of_mind, logic-with-navigation |
| Math | 368 | math_comp (AMC/AIME), olympiad, AMPS_Hard; later integrals-with-game |

| **Total public** | **1,436** | |

- Newer releases (2025-04-25, 2025-11-25, 2026-01-08, 2026-06-25) are **not fully public** on HF. The README says to use release 2024-11-25 for the "most recent public questions".
- 2026 release: 23 tasks in 7 groups, about 40 model variants (from BenchLM mirror; unverified).
- "LiveBench 2.0" (long-horizon agent tasks) is the title on livebench.ai; aggregator DataLearner says it came out in October 2026 (unverified).

## Models
- **In HF judgments (195 models, frozen 2025-04):** newest are Claude 3.7 Sonnet (thinking 64k / base), o3-mini low / medium / high, Qwen2.5-Max, QwQ-32B, Phi-4, Sonar. **No GPT-5, no GPT-6, no Claude 4/5, no Gemini 3/4, no DeepSeek V4.**

  - Google: up to gemini-3.8-flash-high. **No Gemini 4 config found.**
  - DeepSeek: deepseek-v4-pro, v4-pro-0813, v4-flash, v4-flash-0731, v4.1-flash-max, v4.1-flash-1017-max (last commit 2026-10-18).
- **Effort levels:** separate config per effort (low / medium / high / xhigh / max), so scores per effort exist on the site.
- Score tables for Opus 5.5, GPT-6.x and Gemini 4 appear on aggregators (BenchLM, DataLearner, tech-insider), but these are category scores only.

## For Yugos
- **Answer to the key question: no.** Per-question answers for the newest models are **not released**. HF answers stop in 2024-10 and judgments in 2025-04.
- **Overlap:** "LiveBench reasoning" is in Yugos's list. Old public reasoning questions (200) plus math, coding and IF questions are usable.

Sources: [BenchLM LiveBench](https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/livebench), [DataLearner LiveBench 2.0](https://www.datalearner.com/benchmarks/livebench-2-0), [LiveBench changelog](https://github.com/LiveBench/LiveBench/blob/main/changelog.md)

# Router benchmark step 26: SWE-bench experiments repo (2026-11-26)

- Who: SWE-bench team (Princeton / Stanford; John Yang and others). Repo: https://github.com/swe-bench/experiments. Leaderboard: https://www.swebench.com

- Licence: MIT on the SWE-bench code (unverified for this repo). Each submission's logs belong to the submitter.

| Split | Tasks | Submissions in repo | Latest merged |

| Verified | 500 | 182 | 2026-09-01 (mini-SWE-agent v2.4.2 + Gemini 3.5 Flash) |
| Lite | 300 | 84 | 2025-09-11 |

# Router benchmark step 28: tau2-bench (2026-11-26)

- Who: Sierra Research (sierra-research). Repo: https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench. Leaderboard: https://taubench.com
- Data: task files are in the repo under `data/tau2/domains/<domain>/tasks.json`. Licence: MIT.
- Versions: v0.1.x (2025), v0.2.0 (2025-10-06), v1.0.0 "tau3" (2026-03-18; adds `banking_knowledge` and voice), v1.0.1 (2026-07-22; banking grading fix), v2.0.0 (2026-10-20; 6 languages, `intake` domain, post-run "judges").
- Size: 675 base tasks across 5 real domains (telecom also has a 2,285-task full set).
- Format: an agent talks to a simulated user over many turns. The agent uses tools on a mock database. Reward = 1 only if the final database and required actions match. Score = pass^1 (also pass^2–4 over 4 trials).

## Tasks (counted from repo `main`, 2026-11-26)
| Domain | Base tasks | Splits | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| airline | 50 | train 30 / test 20 | flight booking and changes |
| retail | 114 | train 74 / test 40 | orders, returns, exchanges |
| telecom | 114 | train 74 / test 40; small 20; full 2,285 | tech support; user also acts on a phone ("dual control") |
| banking_knowledge | 97 | no split file | knowledge retrieval over ~700 documents; added in tau3 |
| intake (tau-Entity) | 200 | base 200 | new in v2.0; not in Yugos |
| mock | small test domain | — | for testing only |
| **Total (4 Yugos domains)** | **375** | | |

- Yugos v0.3.0 pack used banking 37, telecom 24, retail 14. So Yugos samples a subset of these tasks (the exact task IDs are not checked).
- Voice task files also exist (`tasks_voice.json`) and v2.0 has 50 frozen tasks per domain in 6 languages.

## User simulator
- Text leaderboard (v1.0.1): gpt-5.2 at low reasoning, 4 trials. Older v0.1.3 entries used gpt-4.1.
- Voice: default is now gpt-5.5 (was gpt-4.1). Some voice runs use "user-sim v1.0/v1.1".
- The user model matters. monte-inc saw Gemma 4 go from 11.4% (gpt-4.1 user) to 13.9% (gpt-5.2 user) on banking.
- Some vendor runs used their own model as the user (e.g. Gemini 3 Pro, DeepSeek-V3.2). These are not comparable.

## Leaderboard (89 submission files in `web/leaderboard/public/submissions/`)
- Each `submission.json` has: model, org, date, `reasoning_effort`, pass^1–4 per domain, user simulator, tau2 version.
- Trajectories are not in the repo. They sit on S3: `s3://sierra-tau-bench-public/submissions/<name>/trajectories/` (public access unverified).
- **Text, airline/retail/telecom (v1.0.1, gpt-5.2 user), pass^1:**

  - GPT-5.2 (high): A 83.0, R 81.6, T 89.7

  - Gemini 3 Flash (high): A 82.5, R 76.8, T 91.2
  - Gemini 3 Pro (high): A 80.5, R 75.9, T 91.0
  - Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (thinking): A 81.5, R 84.4, T 97.8
  - GLM-5 (thinking): A 82.5, R 73.7, T 86.8
  - Claude Sonnet 4.5: A 72.0, R 72.4, T 84.9
- **Text, banking_knowledge, pass^1 (newest first):**
  - PrincipledMachines Cortex 0.1 (medium, custom agent, 2026-10-20): 73.2
  - Qwen 3.8 Max (xhigh): 55.2
  - Claude Opus 5 (max): 48.7
  - Grok 4.5 (high): 47.9
  - GPT-5.6-sol (xhigh): 46.9
  - GPT-5.5 (xhigh): 44.6
  - Muse Spark 1.1 (xhigh): 40.5
  - Claude Opus 4.7 (max): 40.2
  - Claude Fable 5 (max) and Opus 4.8 (max): 39.7
  - GPT-5.4 (xhigh): 39.4
  - GLM-5.2 (xhigh) and Kimi K3 (max): 37.1

## Models

- Banking is the hardest domain (best standard model 55%). Yugos's v0.3.0 pack is banking-heavy (37 of 75), so banking skill drives the agentic score.
- Most leaderboard rows are one effort per model (usually high/xhigh/max). There is almost no low/medium data.
- Per-turn routing data: trajectories exist (S3) for v1.0.1 entries. They could show which turns need a strong model (unverified: not downloaded).
- Gap: no scores for the current frontier (GPT-6.x, Opus 5.5, Gemini 4, DeepSeek V4) in text mode. You must run these yourself.
- Results depend on user simulator, tau2 version and harness. Only compare rows with gpt-5.2 user + v1.0.1.

# Router benchmark step 29: Exgentic agent traces (2026-11-26)

- Who: Exgentic ("Open Agent Leaderboard"; blog on HF under ibm-research). Paper: "General Agent Evaluation", https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22953
- Data:
  - Traces: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Exgentic/agent-llm-traces (984 MB, 39 parquet files). Licence: CDLA-Permissive-2.0. Created 2026-05-07, last change 2026-06-07.
  - Scores: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Exgentic/results (150 rows, same licence; copy of `open-agent-leaderboard/results`).
- Size: 1,781 traces (one agent session each). 150 score rows = 5 agents × 5 models × 6 benchmarks.
- Format (traces): OpenTelemetry spans per LLM call. Each span has model, input/output tokens, full input/output messages, tool definitions, finish reason, timing, API status.

## Tasks (traces per benchmark)
| Benchmark | Traces | Tasks per run (results set) | Turns median/mean/max |
|---|---|---|---|
| tau2 retail | 469 | 100 | 8 / 9.1 / 22 |
| tau2 airline | 196 | 50 | 7 / 8.0 / 19 |
| tau2 telecom | 186 | 100 | 15 / 17.3 / 54 |
| AppWorld (test_normal) | 406 | 100 | 14 / 21.4 / 126 |
| SWE-bench (Verified subset, unverified) | 391 | 100 | 35 / 43.6 / 158 |
| BrowseComp+ | 133 | 100 | 19 / 24.6 / 88 |
| **Total** | **1,781** | | |

- No tau2 banking.

## Models (5)
- claude-opus-4-5 (AWS): 509 traces
- gemini-3-pro-preview (GCP): 361
- Kimi-K2.5 (Azure): 160
- DeepSeek-V3.2 (Azure): 135
- gpt-5.2-2025-12-11 (Azure): 52
- (Counts sum to 1,217, not 1,781; the card does not explain the gap.)
- Agents (harnesses): claude_code 839, tool_calling 431, smolagents_code 315, openai_solo 114, tool_calling_with_shortlisting 82.

## Key results (Exgentic/results, success rate, best agent per model)
- tau2 retail: Opus 4.5 0.85 (openai_solo), DeepSeek-V3.2 0.82, Gemini 3 Pro 0.82, GPT-5.2 0.73, Kimi-K2.5 0.72.
- tau2 airline: Opus 4.5 0.74, Gemini 3 Pro 0.70, Kimi-K2.5 0.62, DeepSeek-V3.2 0.60, GPT-5.2 0.60.
- tau2 telecom: Gemini 3 Pro 0.88 (smolagents), DeepSeek-V3.2 0.84, Opus 4.5 0.84, Kimi-K2.5 0.83, GPT-5.2 0.71.
- AppWorld: Opus 4.5 0.70 vs others ≤ 0.57.
- Cost per task differs a lot: tau2 retail with Opus 4.5 ~$0.47–1.60; with DeepSeek-V3.2 ~$0.03–0.05.
- The harness matters as much as the model. Kimi-K2.5 on tau2 telecom: 0.00 (claude_code) vs 0.83 (tool_calling).

## For Yugos
- Covers 3 of Yugos's 4 tau2 domains, plus SWE-bench and AppWorld (both in Yugos's agentic list).
- Good for cost data: tokens per call and per session are recorded. Tau2 sessions use ~100–165k tokens; AppWorld/SWE-bench ~1.2–1.3M.
- Big weakness: the traces have **no task ID and no pass/fail label**. `status` is the API-call status, not task success. Labels exist only as averages in `Exgentic/results`.
- **No reasoning-effort field** in traces or results. All models are early-2026 (Opus 4.5, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro) → not current frontier.
- Use: (1) cheap-vs-strong evidence on tau2 (DeepSeek-V3.2 near Opus 4.5 on retail/telecom at ~1/20 the cost); (2) turn-length and token stats to plan per-turn routing. Not usable as per-question labels (unless traces can be matched to tasks by the first user message — unverified).

|---|---|---|---|
| tau2 banking_knowledge | 97 | 4 (some runs 1) | 388 |

## Models and results (pass rate over all sims; tasks solved ≥1 time)

# Router benchmark step 32: Effort studies (2026-11-26)

- What: 5 small studies that run the **same model at several reasoning-effort levels** and report accuracy per level.
- Collected by: AI Agent Store effort hub, https://aiagentstore.ai/ai-models/reasoning-effort. JSON: https://aiagentstore.ai/data/ai-model-effort-2026-11-23.json (237 KB, v1.2, dated 2026-11-23). Rows = effort, score, cost, latency, tokens.
- All data is **aggregate only** (one score per model × effort). No per-question labels, except joonlab (per-call score tables).
- Size: ~420 tasks across the 5 studies (100 + 200 + 44 + 26 + 50).

## Tasks
| Study | Tasks | Type | Effort levels | Per-task data? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hex DataBench v1.1 | 100 | agentic data analysis in a SQL/notebook workspace (LLM judge) | low, medium, high, xhigh, max | No (task set private) |
| OckBench | 200 (100 math, 60 code, 40 science) | single-turn reasoning; accuracy + tokens | none/off, low, medium, high, xhigh, max | Maybe (HF `ockbench/ockbench`, unverified) |
| joonlab gpt-6.1-sol | 44 math/logic (+1 speed prompt; other tracks 29 code, 53 tool) | Codex (ChatGPT Pro) | medium, high (44 set); low–max (1 prompt) | Yes, per-call scores (CC BY 4.0) |
| Stet | 26 | repo coding (Go, GraphQL-go-tools PRs) in Codex | low, medium, high, xhigh | No download found |
| Hampson | 50 | LiveCodeBench v6 LeetCode | token caps 256 → 12,288, free, off | No download found |

## 1. Hex DataBench v1.1
- Source: https://hex.tech/databench/ ; method: https://hex.tech/blog/databench-agentic-analytics-benchmark/ (2026-08-13).
- 100 tasks (Q&A + open-ended; 10 "signature traps") on a synthetic company warehouse. Judge: GPT-5.6 Sol, majority of 3. v1.1 (2026-09-17) made the judge stricter. Page updated 2026-11-12; 86 model × effort rows.
- Models: Claude Fable 5/5.1, Opus 4.8/5/5.5, Sonnet 5; GPT-5.6 Luna/Sol/Terra; GPT-6 Astra/Luna/Sol; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; GLM 5.2/5.3 (+ xAI, Moonshot on the live page).
- Key results (score %, low → max):
  - Claude Opus 5.5: 54.0 → 62.5 → 65.0 → 67.0 → 70.5. Cost $0.61 → $3.57 per task. Top of board.
  - GPT-6 Astra: 55.0, 52.7, 52.0, 52.3, 55.0 → **flat**; low is as good as max at 40% of the cost.
  - GPT-6 Sol: 50.3 → 61.3 (xhigh) → 57.0 (max). Max is worse than xhigh.
  - GPT-6 Luna: 30.3 → 52.3. Big gain, very cheap ($0.01–0.06 per task).
  - Opus 4.8: 12, 17, 14, 18.7, 15 → noisy, no clear trend. Sonnet 5: max (12.3) below xhigh (14.3).
  - Note: older Claude models (Opus 5, Fable 5) score only 15–20, far below Opus 5.5. Likely the v1.1 judge change (unverified).

## 2. OckBench
- Source: https://ockbench.github.io/ ; code https://github.com/OckBench/OckBench (MIT); paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.05722.
- 200 problems from GSM8K, AIME 24/25, OlympiadBench, MATH500, AMO-Bench, HLE-math; MBPP-lite, LiveCodeBench; ScienceQA, MMLU-STEM, GPQA-Diamond. 56 model settings. Score "OckScore" penalises tokens.
- Key results (accuracy %, tokens):
  - Claude Opus 5: low 85.0 (1.6k tok), medium 85.0, high 94.0 (6.7k), xhigh 95.0, max 94.5 (13.1k). High is the sweet spot.
  - Claude Opus 4.8: low 73.5, medium 86.0, high 86.0, xhigh 91.5, max 90.0 (36.5k tok).
  - GPT-5.5: none 26.0, low 75.0, medium 86.0, high 88.5, xhigh 90.0.
  - GPT-5.4: none 23.5, low 78.0, medium 82.0, high 80.5.
  - DeepSeek V4 Pro: none 25.0, high 84.0, max 84.0 (81k tok). V4 Flash: none 20.5, high 78.0, max 83.0.
  - GLM 5.2: off 28.5, high 78.5, max 83.5. Gemini 3.1 Pro: low 79.5, medium 87.5.
  - Pattern: "none/off" collapses on math (13–17%). Low → medium is the biggest jump. Max rarely beats xhigh.

## 3. joonlab gpt-6.1-sol benchmark
- Source: https://github.com/joonlab/gpt-6.1-sol-benchmark (measured 2026-09-30; CC BY 4.0).
- 7 tracks, 3,527 calls. Effort test: 44 math/logic problems × 2 repeats at medium and high; 1 arithmetic prompt × 3 at low–max.
- Models: GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol/Astra/Luna, GPT-5.6 Sol.
- Key results (44-problem set, medium → high): 6.1 Sol 97.7 → 100; 6 Sol 96.6 → 97.7; 6 Astra 98.9 → 97.7; 6 Luna 81.8 → 86.4.
- Reasoning tokens rise with effort, but no clear accuracy gain (ceiling effect). Latency for 6.1 Sol: ~17.6 s (low) → 53.5 s (max).
- Caveat: ChatGPT subscription, not the API. Small samples.

## 4. Stet (GPT-5.5 Codex reasoning curve)

## For Yugos
- These are the only public sources that put **effort as a column** for current frontier models (GPT-6.x, Opus 5.5).
- Main lesson: more effort is not always better.
  - GPT-6 Astra on DataBench is flat from low to max → route it at low.
  - Max often ties or loses to xhigh/high (GPT-6 Sol, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, OckBench Opus 5).
  - "none/off" is dangerous for math (−50 to −60 points). Low → medium is the most valuable step.
- For agentic tasks (DataBench, Stet), effort helps more for weaker/cheaper models (GPT-6 Luna +22 pts) than for top models.
- Limits: aggregate only, small samples (26–200 tasks), one run per cell, different harnesses. Use as priors for an effort rule, not as training labels.
- None of the studies use tau2, BFCL, Terminal-Bench or AppWorld directly. Yugos agentic effort labels still need own runs.
